chapters.title: Getting Started
text: # Welcome
Every block and item in this world is made of real elements. This guide follows the mod's tech tree from the Stone Age to the last elements, one chapter per level.
# Units

1 unit is 1 gram. A block is 1000 units, an ingot or an element or substance item 111.1, a nugget 12.35 and a bucket 1000. Hover over any block or item to see what it is made of; hold Shift for every part.
# Research

Each level has a research station. Put a project's samples in its 9 slots, pick the project and press Research. Key projects (marked with a star) raise your tech level; you need a level's key projects before you can place the next station. /research shows what you know.
Treatises written at a station teach everything you know to another player.
# Machines

A machine breaks each input item into its composition and runs every reaction you have researched on it while it is hot enough and not too hot. Products come out as items, waste as slag, and some gases are vented. Liquids and gases fill empty Glass Flasks from the machine's side panel. Some reactions need a second ingredient in the reagent slot.

Fire-heated machines burn fuel from the fuel slot: wood reaches 650 °C, charcoal and coal 1100 °C, oil fuels 1200 °C and gas 1300 °C. Bellows (forced air) add 250 °C. Charcoal and coal also serve as the carbon that reduces ores. Electric machines take current from a Voltaic Pile, Dynamo or other power block next to them or joined by Copper Wire.
Vanilla furnaces no longer smelt iron, copper or gold ores: metals come from the machines.
# Level 0
With no research at all you can build a Charcoal Pit (8 dirt round a log) and burn logs into charcoal.

text: # Potter's and Smith's Workshop
Research station for level 1, the Bronze and Iron Age.

@grid periodic_elements:potters_workshop*1|minecraft:brick,minecraft:raw_copper,minecraft:brick/minecraft:charcoal,minecraft:crafting_table,minecraft:charcoal/minecraft:cobblestone,minecraft:cobblestone,minecraft:cobblestone
# Projects (★ = key)
# Fired Pottery (c. 6000 BCE)
Clay fired hot enough to hold liquids and survive a furnace. Samples: 8 Clay Ball, 4 Charcoal. Unlocks Pottery Kiln, Clay firing.
# ★ Copper Smelting (c. 5000 BCE)

Roast copper ore and reduce it with charcoal in a clay furnace; tin ore smelts the same way. Needs Fired Pottery. Samples: 8 Raw Copper, 8 Charcoal. Unlocks Smelting Furnace, Chalcopyrite roasting, Copper oxide reduction, Pyrite roasting, Gold melting, Cassiterite reduction.
# ★ Lime Burning (c. 7000 BCE)
Heat limestone to 900 °C to make quicklime and slaked lime. Needs Fired Pottery. Samples: 8 Calcite or Dripstone Block, 8 Charcoal. Unlocks Lime Kiln, Limestone calcination, Lime Slaking.
# ★ Bronze Alloying (c. 3300 BCE)
Melt copper with about one tenth tin for a harder metal. Needs Copper Smelting. Samples: 8 Copper Ingot, 2 Tin. Unlocks Bronze Ingot, Crucible, Bronze alloying.
# ★ Iron Smelting (c. 1200 BCE)
Reduce iron ore in a charcoal bloomery and hammer out the slag. Needs Bronze Alloying, Bellows. Samples: 16 Raw Iron, 16 Charcoal. Unlocks Bloomery, Iron oxide reduction, Magnetite reduction.
# Bellows (c. 1500 BCE)
Forced air lets furnaces pass 1200 °C. Needs Copper Smelting. Samples: 4 Leather, 8 Oak Planks. Unlocks forced air.
# Salt Evaporation (c. 6000 BCE)

Dry seawater in shallow pans for common salt; the bitter liquor left is bittern. Needs Fired Pottery. Samples: 4 Water Bucket. Unlocks Salt Pan, Brine evaporation, Salt crystallizing, Bucket of Seawater, Sugar crystallizing.
# Fermentation (c. 6000 BCE)

Yeast turns sugar into ethanol in a barrel; in an open vat it sours into vinegar. Needs Fired Pottery. Samples: 8 Wheat, 4 Sugar. Unlocks Fermentation Barrel, Vinegar Vat, Sugar fermentation, Vinegar souring.
# Leavened Bread (c. 4000 BCE)
Sugar-fed dough rises into bread that restores more hunger than vanilla bread. Needs Fermentation. Samples: 16 Wheat. Unlocks Leavened Bread.
# Glassmaking (c. 1500 BCE)
Melt sand with twice its weight of wood ash into forest glass. Needs Lime Burning. Samples: 16 Sand. Unlocks Glass Furnace, Forest glass.
# Writing and Ink (c. 3200 BCE)
Soot ink on paper; lets you write treatises. Samples: 8 Sugar Cane, 2 Charcoal. Unlocks Carbon Ink, Treatise (Manuscript).
# Leather Tanning (c. 5000 BCE)
Soak hides in water with oak bark to make leather. Samples: 4 Rabbit Hide. Unlocks Bark Tanning.
# Cupellation (c. 2500 BCE)

Roast silver-bearing galena on a bone-ash cupel: the lead soaks in as litharge and silver is left. Needs Copper Smelting, Lead Smelting. Samples: 8 Raw Galena, 4 Bone Meal. Unlocks Cupel Hearth, Cupellation.
# Mercury from Cinnabar (c. 500 BCE)
Roast cinnabar to drive off mercury vapour and condense it. Needs Copper Smelting. Samples: 16 Redstone. Unlocks Cinnabar roasting.
# Bronze Tools and Weapons (c. 3000 BCE)
Bronze tools, weapons and armor: better than stone, close to iron. Needs Bronze Alloying. Samples: 2 Tin. Unlocks Bronze Tools and Weapons, Bronze Armor.
# Iron Tools and Weapons (c. 1000 BCE)
Wrought iron tools and armor, tougher than vanilla iron (they replace its recipes). Needs Iron Smelting. Samples: 8 Iron Ingot. Unlocks Wrought Iron Tools, Wrought Iron Armor.
# Lead Smelting (c. 6500 BCE)
Roast galena to litharge and reduce it with charcoal to lead. Needs Copper Smelting. Samples: 8 Raw Galena, 8 Charcoal. Unlocks Galena roasting, Litharge reduction.
# Green Vitriol (c. 100)
Roast pyrite gently in a lime kiln (under 650 °C) for green vitriol. Needs Lime Burning, Copper Smelting. Samples: 16 Cobbled Deepslate, 4 Raw Copper. Unlocks Pyrite sulfation.
# Rendering (c. 3000 BCE)

Simmer meat, fat and bone in a kettle: tallow for candles and soap, and protein meal for the animals. Needs Copper Smelting. Samples: 4 Porkchop, 4 Bone. Unlocks Soap Kettle, Rendering, Greaves, Bone meal rendering, Wax boiling, Tallow Candle.
# Oil Pressing (c. 4000 BCE)
Squeeze seeds in a screw press for oil; the cake left over feeds cattle. Needs Fired Pottery. Samples: 8 Pumpkin Seeds, 8 Wheat Seeds. Unlocks Oil Press, Oil pressing, Jojoba pressing.
# Soap Boiling (c. 2800 BCE)
Boil fat or oil with the potash of wood ash: soft soap, and glycerol in the liquor. Needs Rendering. Samples: 4 Tallow, 4 Wood Ash. Unlocks Soap boiling, Oil soap boiling.
# Pit Tanning (c. 400 BCE)

Lay hides in pits of bark liquor for months: four pieces of flesh make one leather, slowly and without a crafting grid. Needs Leather Tanning. Samples: 8 Rotten Flesh, 4 Oak Log. Unlocks Tanning Pit, Pit tanning.
# Mashing (c. 3500 BCE)
Malt turns the starch of grain and potatoes into sugar, and yeast the sugar into alcohol. Needs Fermentation. Samples: 8 Wheat, 8 Potato. Unlocks Starch mashing, Glucose fermentation.
# Surveying (c. 2300 BCE)

Pace out the land and draw it on a tablet, as at Ga-Sur: the Field Atlas sketches what you walk past, with no coordinates. Needs Writing and Ink. Samples: 8 Paper, 4 Charcoal, 2 Leather. Unlocks Field Atlas, Vanilla Map.
# Domestication (c. 8000 BCE)
Keep the seeds of the best plants: the Seed Lens shows what traits a seed or a crop has. Samples: 16 Wheat Seeds, 8 Carrot. Unlocks Seed Lens.
# Animal Husbandry (c. 7000 BCE)
Pen the herd and feed it: a Feeding Trough feeds the animals around it so they breed and grow. Samples: 4 Hay Block, 16 Wheat. Unlocks Feeding Trough.
# Hide Tent (Prehistory)
Hides on a frame of poles: a Tent you sleep in far from home, which never moves your spawn point. Needs Leather Tanning. Samples: 6 Leather, 4 Stick. Unlocks Tent.
# Leather Backpack (Prehistory)

A leather bag on two straps: a Leather Backpack with 27 places that picks up the plant and mineral specimens you walk over. Needs Leather Tanning. Samples: 8 Leather, 4 String. Unlocks Leather Backpack.
# Hunting Nets (c. 25000 BCE)
A knotted net thrown over game: the Rope Net catches a small animal alive and lets it out where you throw it. Needs Domestication. Samples: 12 String. Unlocks Rope Net.
# Sericulture (c. 2700 BCE)
Silkworms fed on white mulberry leaves spin cocoons; boiled, each gives one long silk thread (Leizu, China). Needs Domestication. Samples: 8 String, 2 White Carpet. Unlocks Sericulture Tray.

text: # Alchemist's Laboratory
Research station for level 2, Alchemy and early modern.

@grid periodic_elements:alchemists_laboratory*1|minecraft:glass,minecraft:iron_ingot,minecraft:glass/minecraft:copper_ingot,periodic_elements:potters_workshop,minecraft:copper_ingot/minecraft:bricks,minecraft:bricks,minecraft:bricks
# Projects (★ = key)
# ★ Alembic Distillation (c. 800)

Boil and condense liquids to purify them; distils wood into wood alcohol and vinegar. Needs Glassmaking, Fermentation. Samples: 8 Glass, 8 Copper Ingot. Unlocks Alembic, Wood distillation, Lignin distillation, Resin distillation, Cinnamon oil, Camphor distillation, Eucalyptol distillation, Santalol distillation, Cedrol distillation, Linalool distillation, Geraniol distillation.
# Desalination (1594)

Boil seawater in a copper still and condense the steam: pure fresh water at sea (Richard Hawkins 1594). Needs Alembic Distillation, Salt Evaporation. Samples: 4 Bucket of Seawater, 4 Copper Ingot. Unlocks Seawater Still, Desalination, Still salt.
# ★ Mineral Acids (c. 1300)

Distil green vitriol and saltpetre into sulfuric and nitric acids; salt and acid give hydrochloric acid. Needs Alembic Distillation. Samples: 4 Iron(II) Sulfate, 4 Potassium Nitrate. Unlocks Oil of vitriol, Aqua fortis, Spirit of salt.
# ★ Saltpetre Refining (c. 1250)
Leach nitre beds and recrystallise potassium nitrate. Needs Alembic Distillation. Samples: 16 Dirt, 8 Bone Meal. Unlocks Crystallizer, Saltpeter leaching.
# ★ Blast Furnace (c. 1150)

A tall furnace that melts iron fully for casting. Needs Iron Smelting. Samples: 16 Iron Ingot, 16 Bricks. Unlocks Charcoal Blast Furnace, Cast iron, Cast iron magnetite, Cast Iron Ingot, Refractory Brick, Tuyere, Structure Port.
# Black Powder (c. 850 (China))
Saltpetre with charcoal and sulfur. Needs Saltpetre Refining. Samples: 4 Potassium Nitrate, 2 Sulfur. Unlocks Black Powder, Hand Cannon.
# Aqua Regia (c. 1300)
Nitric plus hydrochloric acid dissolves gold for purification. Needs Mineral Acids. Samples: 2 Gold Ingot. Unlocks Aqua Regia, Gold dissolution.
# Zinc Distillation (c. 1300)

Reduce zinc ore in a closed retort and condense the metal; makes brass. Needs Alembic Distillation. Samples: 8 Raw Sphalerite. Unlocks Zinc Retort, Sphalerite roasting, Zinc oxide reduction, Brass alloying, Brass Ingot.
# Printing Press (1440)
Movable type of lead-tin-antimony alloy; lets you print treatises. Needs Writing and Ink, Antimony. Samples: 4 Iron Ingot, 4 Lead. Unlocks Treatise (Printed), Type Metal, Type metal alloying.
# Iron-Gall Ink (c. 1100)
Permanent ink from oak galls and green vitriol. Needs Mineral Acids. Samples: 2 Iron(II) Sulfate. Unlocks Iron-Gall Ink.
# Porcelain (1708)
Kaolin fired at 1300 °C into hard white crucibles and labware. Needs Blast Furnace. Samples: 16 Clay Ball. Unlocks Porcelain Kiln, Porcelain, Kaolin firing.
# Ground Lenses (1286)
A magnifying lens shows what the block you look at is made of. Needs Glassmaking. Samples: 4 Glass. Unlocks Magnifying Lens.
# Phosphorus (1669)
Distil phosphorus from bone ash or urine residue. Needs Alembic Distillation. Samples: 16 Bone Meal. Unlocks Phosphorus Retort, Phosphorus from bones.
# Mercury Amalgamation (1554)
Extract silver from ore with mercury. Needs Mercury from Cinnabar. Samples: 1 Mercury. Unlocks Amalgamation Pan, Silver amalgamation, Gold amalgamation.
# Cementation Steel (c. 1600)

Pack wrought iron in charcoal for days to make blister steel for tools and armor. Needs Blast Furnace. Samples: 16 Iron Ingot, 16 Charcoal. Unlocks Cementation Furnace, Iron cementation, Steel Ingot, Steel Tools, Steel Armor.
# White Arsenic (c. 1250)

Roast arsenopyrite in a reverberatory furnace, catch the white arsenic and reduce it with charcoal (Albertus Magnus). Needs Alembic Distillation. Samples: 8 Raw Arsenopyrite, 8 Charcoal. Unlocks Reverberatory Furnace, Arsenopyrite roasting, Arsenic reduction.
# Antimony (1540)
Roast stibnite to its oxide and reduce it with charcoal (Biringuccio, 1540). Needs White Arsenic. Samples: 8 Raw Stibnite, 8 Charcoal. Unlocks Stibnite roasting, Antimony reduction.
# Bismuth (c. 1500)
Bismuth melts at 271 °C and runs out of Saxon cobalt ore. Needs White Arsenic. Samples: 8 Raw Cobaltite. Unlocks Bismuth liquation.
# Cobalt (1735)

Brandt shows that the blue of cobalt glass comes from a new metal: roast cobaltite and reduce the oxide. Needs Bismuth. Samples: 16 Raw Cobaltite, 8 Charcoal. Unlocks Cobaltite roasting, Cobalt reduction.
# Sweet Oil of Vitriol (1540)
Distil spirit with a little oil of vitriol: diethyl ether, a solvent and a fuel (Cordus). Needs Mineral Acids, Fermentation. Samples: 4 Ethanol, 2 Sulfuric Acid. Unlocks Ether distillation.
# Alum Making (1754)

Dissolve clay in oil of vitriol and add potash: alum crystals, which taw rabbit hide into leather (Marggraf). Needs Mineral Acids, Saltpetre Refining. Samples: 8 Clay Ball, 4 Sulfuric Acid. Unlocks Clay sulfation, Alum crystallization, Alum Tawing.
# Hard Soap (c. 800)

Soda ash or a handful of salt makes soap that sets in hard bars (Aleppo, Castile). Needs Soap Boiling, Salt Evaporation. Samples: 4 Soft Soap, 4 Sodium Chloride. Unlocks Hard soap boiling, Soap salting.
# Prussian Blue (1706)

Blood calcined with potash and struck with green vitriol: the first synthetic pigment, made in a Dye Vat (Diesbach). Needs Alum Making, Green Vitriol. Samples: 8 Rotten Flesh, 4 Iron(II) Sulfate. Unlocks Dye Vat, Prussiate making, Blue dyeing, Brazilin dyeing, Bixin dyeing, Lawsone dyeing.
# Quarry Hammers (c. 1800)

Quarrymen's sledges and navvies' broad shovels: a Sledgehammer breaks 3x3 of stone and an Excavator 3x3 of earth, slowly, at one wear per block. Needs Cementation Steel. Samples: 4 Steel Ingot, 16 Cobblestone. Unlocks Sledgehammers, Excavators.
# Rock Blasting (1627)

Black powder packed into a drilled hole (Schemnitz 1627): a Blasting Charge breaks a 3x3x3 block of stone, drops all of it and never harms a machine. Needs Black Powder. Samples: 4 Black Powder, 16 Cobblestone. Unlocks Blasting Charge.
# Magnetic Compass (c. 1190)

A magnetised needle points north: the Atlas shows north, your exact place and facing, and a compass bar while you hold it. Needs Surveying, Iron Tools and Weapons. Samples: 4 Iron Ingot, 4 Redstone. Unlocks Compass, Vanilla Compass.
# Quadrant and Astrolabe (c. 1300)

Measure the height of the pole star and you know how far north you are: the Atlas shows Z, a scale bar, and draws twice as far. Needs Magnetic Compass. Samples: 4 Bronze Ingot, 4 Paper. Unlocks Latitude.
# Portolan Charts (c. 1300)

Sailors copied each other's coastlines: sneak and use the Atlas with paper in your other hand to make an Atlas Copy for someone else. Needs Quadrant and Astrolabe, Iron-Gall Ink. Samples: 16 Paper, 2 Iron-Gall Ink. Unlocks Copy.
# De re metallica (1556)

Agricola describes every ore and how miners find it: the Mineral Compendium shows each ore's mineral and the depths where it is found. Needs Ground Lenses, Writing and Ink. Samples: 8 Paper, 4 Raw Iron, 4 Raw Copper. Unlocks Ores.
# Heated Greenhouse (1681)

Glass houses warmed by a stove (Chelsea Physic Garden 1681): tropical and desert plants grow far from home. Needs Glassmaking, Alembic Distillation. Samples: 8 Glass, 8 Brick. Unlocks Greenhouse Heater.
# Crop Rotation (c. 800)
Three-field rotation: soybeans, beans, indigo and alfalfa leave the ground fertilized when harvested. Needs Domestication. Samples: 8 Beans or Soybeans, 8 Bone Meal. Unlocks Rotation.
# Natural Dyes (c. 1200)
Blue from indigo, red from madder root: the Dye Vat dyes with plants. Needs Domestication. Samples: 8 Indigo Leaves, 8 Madder Root. Unlocks Indigo dyeing, Madder dyeing.
# Explorer's Compass (c. 1500)
Bearings and travellers' accounts: choose a biome and the Explorer's Compass points to the nearest one. Needs Magnetic Compass, Portolan Charts. Samples: 1 Compass, 2 Map. Unlocks Explorer's Compass.
# Carmine (c. 1520)
The Aztecs' crimson of dried cochineal, shipped to Europe by Spain: dye red in a Dye Vat with cochineal. Needs Prussian Blue. Samples: 8 Cactus, 4 Red Dye. Unlocks Carmine dyeing.
# Tyrian Purple (c. 1500 BCE)
The Phoenicians' purple from murex snails, worth more than gold: dye purple in a Dye Vat with murex. Needs Prussian Blue. Samples: 4 Purple Dye, 4 Prismarine Shard. Unlocks Tyrian purple dyeing.

text: # Natural Philosopher's Laboratory
Research station for level 3, the Chemical Revolution.

@grid periodic_elements:natural_philosophers_laboratory*1|minecraft:glass,periodic_elements:brass_ingot,minecraft:glass/periodic_elements:steel_ingot,periodic_elements:alchemists_laboratory,periodic_elements:steel_ingot/minecraft:bricks,minecraft:bricks,minecraft:bricks
# Projects (★ = key)

Bake coal into coke: a fuel hot enough to melt steel. Needs Blast Furnace. Samples: 16 Coal, 8 Charcoal. Unlocks Coke Oven, Coal coking, Coal degassing hydrogen, Coal degassing oxygen, Coal degassing nitrogen, Coal degassing sulfur, Silica Brick.
# ★ Crucible Steel (1740)

Melt blister steel in a closed crucible at 1600 °C for even steel; the best blades before electricity. Needs Coke, Cementation Steel. Samples: 8 Steel Ingot, 4 Coke. Unlocks Huntsman Crucible Furnace, Crucible steel, Crucible Steel Tools, Crucible Steel Armor.
# ★ Steam Engine (1712)
A coal-fired engine that drives blowing cylinders: furnaces next to it burn 200 °C hotter. Needs Coke. Samples: 8 Cast Iron Ingot, 4 Copper Ingot. Unlocks Steam Engine, steam blast.
# ★ Pneumatic Chemistry (1766)

Collect gases under water: hydrogen from iron and acid; oxygen and nitrogen from red-hot saltpetre. Needs Mineral Acids. Samples: 8 Glass, 2 Mercury. Unlocks Pneumatic Trough, Hydrogen from iron, Nitre decomposition, Storage Tank.
# ★ Voltaic Pile (1800)
Discs of zinc and copper in brine or acid: the first steady electric current. Needs Zinc Distillation, Mineral Acids. Samples: 8 Zinc, 8 Copper Ingot. Unlocks Voltaic Pile.
# ★ Electrolysis (1807)
Split molten salts and water with current: sodium. Needs Voltaic Pile. Samples: 4 Sodium Chloride, 4 Zinc. Unlocks Electrolysis Cell, Salt electrolysis, Sylvite electrolysis, Water electrolysis.
# ★ Lead Chamber Process (1746)

Burn sulfur or pyrite into a lead room with steam: sulfuric acid by the barrel. Needs Mineral Acids, Lead Smelting. Samples: 8 Lead, 8 Sulfur. Unlocks Lead Chamber, Lead Sheet, Gay-Lussac Tower, Sulfur chamber acid, Pyrite chamber acid.
# Alkaline Earth Metals (1808)

Calcium, magnesium, barium and strontium by electrolysis of their earths and of bittern. Needs Electrolysis. Samples: 4 Calcium Oxide, 4 Raw Barite. Unlocks Lime electrolysis, Magnesium electrolysis, Baryta electrolysis, Strontia electrolysis, Barite reduction, Celestine reduction.
# Acid Digestion (c. 1790)

Dissolve ores in hot acid in porcelain-lined vats; borax gives boric acid. Needs Mineral Acids, Porcelain. Samples: 4 Sulfuric Acid, 4 Porcelain. Unlocks Digestion Vat, Borax leaching, Quinine extraction, Salicin extraction, Citric acid crystallizing.
# Lithium (1817)
Leach spodumene for lithium chloride and electrolyse it (Arfwedson; Bunsen). Needs Acid Digestion, Electrolysis. Samples: 8 Raw Spodumene. Unlocks Spodumene leaching, Lithium electrolysis.
# Boron (1808)
Strip the oxygen from boric acid with potassium in a sealed crucible. Needs Acid Digestion, Electrolysis. Samples: 8 Raw Borax. Unlocks Reduction Crucible, Boron reduction.
# Beryllium (1828)
Chlorinate beryl and reduce the chloride with potassium (Wohler). Needs Boron. Samples: 4 Emerald. Unlocks Beryl chlorination, Beryllium reduction.
# Selenium (1817)
Distil selenium out of lead-chamber sludge (Berzelius). Needs Lead Chamber Process. Samples: 4 Chamber Sludge. Unlocks Selenium sublimation.
# Bromine (1826)
Free bromine from bittern with chlorine (Balard). Needs Electrolysis, Salt Evaporation. Samples: 2 Chlorine, 2 Water Bucket. Unlocks Bromine liberation.
# Iodine (1811)
Violet vapour from kelp ash and oil of vitriol (Courtois). Needs Mineral Acids. Samples: 16 Dried Kelp. Unlocks Iodine from kelp.
# Cadmium (1817)
Catch the cadmium that distils from zinc ore before the zinc (Stromeyer). Needs Zinc Distillation. Samples: 8 Raw Sphalerite. Unlocks Greenockite roasting, Cadmium reduction.
# Platinum (1803)
Dissolve platinum grains from gold ore in aqua regia and press the sponge (Wollaston). Needs Aqua Regia. Samples: 8 Raw Gold. Unlocks Platinum dissolution.
# Uranium Oxide (1789)
Roast pitchblende for the black oxide Klaproth named uranium. Needs Mineral Acids. Samples: 4 Raw Pitchblende. Unlocks Pitchblende roasting.
# Flintlock Musket (c. 1610)

A steel-barrelled musket fired by flint: harder hitting and quicker to reload than the hand cannon. Needs Crucible Steel, Black Powder. Samples: 4 Crucible Steel Ingot, 4 Flint. Unlocks Flintlock Musket.
# Automatic Mill (1785)

Oliver Evans' mill moves grain from step to step with no hand on it: an Output Pusher moves a machine's products into the chest next to it. Needs Steam Engine. Samples: 2 Hopper, 2 Piston. Unlocks Output Pusher, output pusher, Canvas Belt.
# Gas Mains (1812)

Winsor and Clegg lit London with coal gas sent through iron mains from gasholders (1812): Fluid Pipes join machines to tanks, and Tank Plates build a tank as big as you like. Needs Pneumatic Chemistry, Steam Engine. Samples: 8 Iron Ingot, 4 Lead. Unlocks Tank Plate, Tank Controller, Tank Valve, Tank Gauge, Fluid Pipe, Fluid Pump.
# Gas Liquor (1840)

Wash the ammonia out of coke-oven gas and neutralise it with acid: sulfate of ammonia for the fields. Needs Coke, Lead Chamber Process. Samples: 16 Coal, 4 Sulfuric Acid. Unlocks Ammonia liquor, Ammonium sulfate making.
# Superphosphate (1842)
Dissolve bones or phosphate rock in sulfuric acid: the first factory fertilizer (Lawes). Needs Acid Digestion. Samples: 8 Bone Meal, 4 Sulfuric Acid. Unlocks Superphosphate making.
# Starch Sugar (1811)
Boil starch with a little acid and it becomes sugar, faster than malt (Kirchhoff). Needs Acid Digestion, Mashing. Samples: 16 Potato, 2 Sulfuric Acid. Unlocks Starch hydrolysis.
# Vulcanization (1839)

Tap latex from rubber trees in the jungle and cure the rubber with sulfur: tough, springy and waterproof (Goodyear). Needs Steam Engine. Samples: 8 Sulfur, 4 Jungle Log. Unlocks Vulcanizer, Vulcanization, Latex drying, Tree Tap, Sneakers, Rubber Wheels.
# Tar Distillation (1848)

Catch the tar of the coke oven and cut it in a still: benzene, carbolic acid, anthracene, and pitch for tarmac (Mansfield). Needs Coke, Alembic Distillation. Samples: 16 Coal, 4 Coke. Unlocks Tar Still, Coal tar condensing, Tar distillation, Tarmac.
# Nitrobenzene (1834)
Benzene stirred into nitric and sulfuric acid: oil of mirbane, the way to aniline (Mitscherlich). Needs Tar Distillation, Acid Digestion. Samples: 2 Benzene, 2 Nitric Acid. Unlocks Benzene nitration.
# Marine Chronometer (1761)

Harrison's H4 keeps time at sea, and the time difference gives longitude: the Atlas shows X as well. Needs Quadrant and Astrolabe, Crucible Steel. Samples: 4 Crucible Steel Ingot, 2 Gold Ingot. Unlocks Longitude.
# Hot-Air Balloon (1783)

The Montgolfiers' balloon lifts an observer above the land: a Survey Balloon draws 128 blocks all round at once. Needs Surveying, Pneumatic Chemistry. Samples: 16 White Wool, 8 String. Unlocks Survey Balloon.
# Triangulation and Theodolite (1787)

Ramsden's great theodolite measures angles to a fraction of a second: the Atlas draws sharp, with relief shading and contour lines every 8 blocks. Needs Marine Chronometer, Ground Lenses. Samples: 4 Brass Ingot, 4 Glass. Unlocks Contours.
# Geological Map (1815)

William Smith coloured England by the rock beneath the soil: the Atlas gains a layer showing the bedrock under every column you walk past. Needs Triangulation and Theodolite. Samples: 8 Granite, 8 Diorite, 8 Andesite. Unlocks Geology.
# Species Plantarum (1753)

Linnaeus counted stamens with a hand lens and gave every plant two Latin names: the Tree Compendium shows each tree's scientific name, family and native range. Needs Ground Lenses, Writing and Ink. Samples: 8 Paper, 8 Oak Sapling or Birch Sapling or Spruce Sapling or Jungle Sapling or Acacia Sapling or Dark Oak Sapling or Cherry Sapling. Unlocks Classification.
# Geography of Plants (1807)

Humboldt carried a barometer and thermometer up Chimborazo and saw the forests change with height and heat: the Compendium shows each biome's climate. Needs Species Plantarum, Pneumatic Chemistry. Samples: 8 Paper, 2 Glass Bottle. Unlocks Climate.
# Theory of the Earth (1788)

Hutton reads at Siccar Point that rocks are made, worn away and made again: the Compendium sorts rocks into igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic and names the formation underfoot. Needs De re metallica, Geological Map. Samples: 8 Paper, 4 Granite, 4 Sandstone, 4 Basalt. Unlocks Origin.
# Plant Hybridization (1761)
Kölreuter crossed tobacco plants by hand: the Pollination Brush chooses the father of a plant's seeds. Needs Domestication. Samples: 4 Feather, 16 Maize Kernels. Unlocks Pollination Brush.
# Tobacco Wash (1763)
Tobacco steeped in water kills caterpillars on crops: the first insecticide of the farm. Needs Domestication. Samples: 8 Tobacco Leaves, 4 Glass Bottle. Unlocks Tobacco Wash.
# Animal Cage (1752)
The menageries' travelling cages: the Steel Cage carries any animal, a horse or a cow too, and never wears out. Needs Crucible Steel. Samples: 8 Iron Bars, 2 Crucible Steel Ingot. Unlocks Steel Cage.
# Shellac (c. 1750)

Sticklac scraped from Indian trees, washed and melted: shellac, varnish for furniture and the insulation of early electricity. Needs Rendering. Samples: 16 Stick, 2 Honeycomb. Unlocks Shellac refining.
# Guano (1840)

Peruvian seabird guano, leached with hot water and potash: saltpetre for powder and fields (the Guano Age, 1840-1880). Needs Saltpetre Refining. Samples: 8 Bone Meal, 8 Feather. Unlocks Guano saltpetre.

- Salicin extraction: 100 Salicin -> 100 Salicin. 20 to 100 °C.
- Citric acid crystallizing: 100 Citric Acid -> 100 Citric Acid. 20 to 100 °C.
- Guano saltpetre: 100 Potassium Nitrate -> 100 Potassium Nitrate. 60 to 100 °C.
# Reduction Crucible
- Boron reduction: 100 Boric Acid + 189.7 Potassium (reagent) -> 17.48 Boron; slag: Potassium Oxide; vents Water. 600 to 1000 °C.
- Beryllium reduction: 100 Beryllium Chloride + 97.85 Potassium (reagent) -> 11.28 Beryllium, 186.58 Potassium Chloride. 600 to 1000 °C.
# Lead Chamber
- Sulfur chamber acid: 100 Sulfur + 56.19 Water (reagent) -> 305.9 Sulfuric Acid, 2 Chamber Sludge. 40 to 150 °C.
- Pyrite chamber acid: 100 Pyrite + 30.03 Water (reagent) -> 163.5 Sulfuric Acid, 10 Chamber Sludge; slag: Iron(III) Oxide. 40 to 150 °C.
- Ammonium sulfate making: 100 Ammonia Water + 140 Sulfuric Acid (reagent) -> 188.6 Ammonium Sulfate; vents Water. 20 to 100 °C.
# Alembic
- Bromine liberation: 100 Magnesium Bromide + 38.51 Chlorine (reagent) -> 51.71 Magnesium Chloride, 86.8 Bromine. 59 to 200 °C.
- Iodine from kelp: 100 Sodium Iodide + 98.14 Sulfuric Acid (reagent) -> 84.66 Iodine; slag: Sodium Bisulfate; vents Sulfur Dioxide, Water. 100 to 250 °C.
- Platinum dissolution: 100 Platinum + 64.6 Nitric Acid (reagent), 129.2 Hydrochloric Acid (reagent) -> 100 Platinum; vents Acid Fumes. 20 to 110 °C.
# Zinc Retort
- Greenockite roasting: 100 Greenockite -> 88.88 Cadmium Oxide; vents Sulfur Dioxide. 600 to 1350 °C.
- Cadmium reduction: 100 Cadmium Oxide + 9.35 carbon -> 87.54 Cadmium; vents Carbon Monoxide. 700 to 1350 °C.
# Vulcanizer
- Vulcanization: 100 Natural Rubber + 3 Sulfur (reagent) -> 103 Vulcanized Rubber. 130 to 160 °C.
- Latex drying: 100 Natural Rubber -> 100 Natural Rubber. 130 to 160 °C.
# Tar Still
- Tar distillation: 100 Coal Tar -> 15 Benzene, 5 Toluene, 10 Phenol, 8 Anthracene; slag: Coal Tar Pitch. 170 to 400 °C.
# Soap Kettle
- Shellac refining: 100 Shellac -> 100 Shellac. 80 to 150 °C.

text: # Industrial Research Laboratory
Research station for level 4, industrial chemistry.

@grid periodic_elements:industrial_laboratory*1|minecraft:glass,periodic_elements:crucible_steel_ingot,minecraft:glass/minecraft:copper_ingot,periodic_elements:natural_philosophers_laboratory,minecraft:copper_ingot/periodic_elements:steel_ingot,periodic_elements:steel_ingot,periodic_elements:steel_ingot
# Projects (★ = key)
# ★ Dynamo (1866)

A self-exciting dynamo driven by a steam engine: current by the kilowatt, carried on copper wire (Siemens 1866). Needs Electrolysis, Steam Engine. Samples: 16 Copper Ingot, 8 Iron Ingot. Unlocks Dynamo, Copper Wire.
# ★ Bessemer Converter (1856)

Blow air through molten pig iron: its own carbon burns and keeps it molten; steel by the tonne. Needs Crucible Steel, Steam Engine. Samples: 16 Cast Iron Ingot, 8 Coke. Unlocks Bessemer Converter, Bessemer decarburization, Bessemer steel.
# ★ Chlor-Alkali Process (1892)
Electrolyse brine over a mercury cathode: lye, chlorine and hydrogen (Castner and Kellner). Needs Dynamo. Samples: 8 Sodium Chloride, 4 Mercury. Unlocks Chlor-Alkali Cell, Brine electrolysis.
# ★ Liquid Air (1895)

Compress and cool air until it is liquid, then boil off nitrogen, argon and oxygen in turn (Linde). Needs Dynamo, Pneumatic Chemistry. Samples: 8 Copper Ingot, 4 Crucible Steel Ingot. Unlocks Air Liquefier, Nitrogen fraction, Oxygen fraction, Argon fraction.
# ★ Spectroscopy (1859)

Every element colours a flame with its own lines: a prism finds traces no balance can (Bunsen and Kirchhoff). Needs Ground Lenses, Alembic Distillation. Samples: 8 Glass, 4 Brass Ingot. Unlocks Spectroscope Bench, Bench zinc oxide, Bench selenium.
# ★ Electrolytic Refining (1869)

Refine copper by current; the slime under the anodes holds the precious metals and tellurium. Needs Dynamo. Samples: 16 Copper Ingot, 8 Lead. Unlocks Electrolytic Refinery, Copper refining, Slime silver, Slime gold, Slime selenium, Slime tellurium.
# ★ Hall-Heroult Process (1886)

Dissolve alumina in molten cryolite and split it with current: aluminium becomes cheaper than silver. Needs Bayer Process. Samples: 8 Aluminium Oxide, 4 Raw Fluorite. Unlocks Hall-Heroult Cell, Alumina electrolysis, Cryolite washing, Aluminium Tools, Aluminium Armor.
# Neon, Krypton and Xenon (1898)

Boil liquid air slowly and read each fraction in the spectroscope (Ramsay and Travers). Needs Liquid Air, Spectroscopy. Samples: 2 Argon, 4 Glass. Unlocks Neon fraction, Krypton fraction, Xenon fraction, Helium fraction.
# Caesium and Rubidium (1861)

The first elements found by spectrum: in the lithium liquor of pegmatite. Needs Spectroscopy, Lithium. Samples: 16 Raw Spodumene. Unlocks Rubidium leaching, Caesium leaching, Rubidium electrolysis, Caesium electrolysis.
# Indium (1863)
An indigo line in zinc ore: catch indium in the retort flue dust. Needs Spectroscopy, Cadmium. Samples: 16 Raw Sphalerite. Unlocks Indium fuming, Bench indium, Indium electrolysis.
# Germanium (1886)

Mendeleev's eka-silicon, found where he said it would be; reduce its oxide with hydrogen (Winkler). Needs Indium, Pneumatic Chemistry. Samples: 16 Raw Sphalerite, 2 Hydrogen. Unlocks Germanium fuming, Bench germanium, Germanium reduction.
# Thallium (1861)
A bright green line in lead-chamber sludge (Crookes). Needs Spectroscopy, Selenium. Samples: 8 Chamber Sludge. Unlocks Bench thallium, Thallium electrolysis.
# Platinum Group Metals (1844)

Part anode slime with aqua regia into platinum, palladium and rhodium; the black residue holds ruthenium, osmium and iridium. Needs Electrolytic Refining, Platinum. Samples: 4 Anode Slime, 4 Aqua Regia. Unlocks Slime platinum, Slime palladium, Slime rhodium, Slime ruthenium, Slime osmium, Slime iridium.
# Bayer Process (1888)

Dissolve the alumina out of bauxite with hot lye under pressure and leave the iron behind as red mud. Needs Chlor-Alkali Process, Acid Digestion. Samples: 8 Raw Bauxite, 4 Sodium Hydroxide. Unlocks Bayer Digester, Gibbsite digestion.
# Gallium (1875)
Draw gallium from the Bayer liquor: a metal that melts in your hand. Needs Bayer Process, Spectroscopy. Samples: 16 Raw Bauxite. Unlocks Gallium liquor, Gallium electrolysis.
# Fluorine (1886)

Hydrogen fluoride from fluorspar, electrolysed in platinum: the most reactive element, isolated at last (Moissan). Needs Chlor-Alkali Process, Acid Digestion. Samples: 8 Raw Fluorite, 2 Platinum. Unlocks Moissan Cell, Fluorite digestion, Hf electrolysis.
# Manganese Steel (1882)

Ferromanganese from pyrolusite; steel with 12% manganese grows harder where it is struck (Hadfield). Needs Bessemer Converter. Samples: 8 Raw Pyrolusite. Unlocks Pyrolusite reduction, Manganese steel, Manganese Steel Tools, Manganese Steel Armor.
# Solvay Process (1861)
Soda ash from salt and limestone with ammonia as the go-between. Needs Alkaline Earth Metals. Samples: 8 Sodium Chloride, 4 Calcite. Unlocks Solvay Tower, Solvay soda.
# Tungsten Steel (1868)

Tungsten from wolframite; Mushet's tungsten steel holds its edge when red hot. Needs Manganese Steel, Solvay Process. Samples: 8 Raw Wolframite, 4 Sodium Carbonate. Unlocks Wolframite roasting, Tungstate precipitation, Tungsten reduction, Tungsten steel, Tungsten Steel Tools.
# Vanadium (1867)

Vanadium oxide from vanadinite; reduce it with burning aluminium (Roscoe; Goldschmidt). Needs Solvay Process, Hall-Heroult Process. Samples: 8 Raw Vanadinite, 2 Aluminium. Unlocks Vanadinite roasting, Vanadate precipitation, Vanadium thermite.
# Contact Process (1875)
Sulfur dioxide over a hot catalyst: strong sulfuric acid by the tonne. Needs Lead Chamber Process, Vanadium. Samples: 4 Sulfuric Acid, 2 Vanadium Pentoxide. Unlocks Contact Converter, Contact acid.
# Mond Process (1890)
Carbon monoxide carries nickel off as a gas and lays it down pure (Mond). Needs Coke, Mineral Acids. Samples: 8 Raw Pentlandite, 4 Coke. Unlocks Mond Reactor, Pentlandite roasting, Nickel carbonyl.
# Radioactivity (1896)

Uranium salts discharge a gold-leaf electroscope through paper: invisible rays (Becquerel). Needs Uranium Oxide, Spectroscopy. Samples: 4 Raw Pitchblende, 2 Gold Ingot. Unlocks Gold-Leaf Electroscope.
# Helium (1895)
The gas from uranium ore shows the yellow line seen only in the sun (Ramsay). Needs Spectroscopy, Uranium Oxide. Samples: 8 Raw Pitchblende, 4 Glass. Unlocks Helium release.
# Radium (1898)

Follow the activity through tonnes of pitchblende residue to a gram of radium (Marie and Pierre Curie). Needs Radioactivity, Alkaline Earth Metals. Samples: 16 Raw Pitchblende, 4 Raw Barite. Unlocks Residue radium, Residue polonium, Residue actinium, Radium conversion, Radium electrolysis.
# Polonium (1898)
The first element found by its radioactivity; named for Poland. Needs Radium. Samples: 2 Pitchblende Residue. Unlocks Polonium separation.
# Actinium (1899)
Debierne's ray-giving element from the rare-earth part of the residue. Needs Radium. Samples: 2 Pitchblende Residue. Unlocks Actinium separation.
# Radon (1900)
Radium gives off a radioactive gas: pump it off and seal it in gold seeds (Dorn). Needs Radium, Pneumatic Chemistry. Samples: 1 Radium Chloride, 2 Gold Ingot. Unlocks Radon collection.
# Helium from Radium (1903)
Radium sealed in a tube slowly fills it with helium: alpha rays are helium (Ramsay and Soddy, Rutherford). Needs Helium, Radium. Samples: 16 Raw Pitchblende, 4 Glass Flask. Unlocks Helium Collector.
# Thorium (1829)

Thorium from the black sand of beaches: dissolve its oxide and reduce the chloride with potassium (Berzelius). Needs Boron, Acid Digestion. Samples: 8 Heavy Mineral Concentrate, 2 Potassium. Unlocks Thorianite chlorination, Thorium reduction.
# Smokeless Powder (1884)
Guncotton gelled into a powder that burns without smoke and three times as strong (Vieille). Needs Mineral Acids, Lead Chamber Process. Samples: 4 Nitric Acid, 8 Paper. Unlocks Cellulose nitration.
# Breech-Loading Rifle (1886)

A steel rifle loaded from the back with brass cartridges of smokeless powder (Lebel). Needs Smokeless Powder, Manganese Steel. Samples: 4 Manganese Steel Ingot, 4 Brass Ingot. Unlocks Breech-Loading Rifle.
# ★ Oil Refining (1859)

Retort oil shale in an alembic and distil the crude oil into naphtha, kerosene, diesel and bitumen (Young 1851, Drake 1859); bitumen binds asphalt roads. Needs Alembic Distillation, Bessemer Converter. Samples: 16 Raw Oil Shale, 8 Coal. Unlocks Oil Refinery Still, Distillation Tray, Shale retorting, Crude distillation, Asphalt.
# Diesel Engine (1897)
Diesel's compression-ignition engine turns a generator: current from oil with no boiler or water. Needs Oil Refining, Dynamo. Samples: 4 Diesel, 8 Steel Ingot. Unlocks Diesel Generator.
# Gas Compression (1885)

Seamless drawn steel cylinders hold gas at 150 atmospheres (Mannesmann 1885): a Compressor upgrade lets a machine fill them, nine flasks to a cylinder. Needs Bessemer Converter, Pneumatic Chemistry. Samples: 8 Steel Ingot, 2 Piston. Unlocks Steel Cylinder, Compressor, compressor, Tank Compressor.
# Regenerative Furnace (1856)

Siemens passes the hot flue gas through brick checkerwork that then heats the incoming air: a Regenerator upgrade halves a fuel-fired machine's heat loss. Needs Bessemer Converter. Samples: 16 Bricks, 8 Cast Iron Ingot. Unlocks Regenerator, regenerator.
# Basic Refractories (1878)

Thomas and Gilchrist line the converter with burnt lime and dolomite that stand the heat and the slag: a Refractory Lining lets a fuel-fired machine run 150 °C hotter. Needs Bessemer Converter, Lime Burning. Samples: 16 Bricks, 8 Calcium Oxide. Unlocks Refractory Lining, refractory lining.
# By-Product Recovery (1881)

By-product coke ovens catch the gas instead of burning it off: a Gas Recovery Hood bottles the gases a machine vents. Needs Coke, Gas Compression. Samples: 8 Coke, 8 Glass. Unlocks Gas Recovery Hood, gas recovery hood.
# Electric Motor (1888)

Tesla's induction motor turns a paddle in the vessel: a Mechanical Stirrer makes a machine work 50% faster for a quarter more fuel or current. Needs Dynamo. Samples: 8 Copper Wire, 8 Iron Ingot. Unlocks Mechanical Stirrer, mechanical stirrer.
# Aniline (1854)
Reduce nitrobenzene with iron filings and a little acid: aniline, the base of the coal tar dyes (Bechamp). Needs Nitrobenzene. Samples: 4 Nitrobenzene, 4 Iron Ingot. Unlocks Aniline reduction.
# Fuchsine (1858)
Aniline and arsenic acid give magenta, the dye that made the aniline fortunes (Verguin). Needs Aniline, Prussian Blue. Samples: 2 Aniline, 2 White Arsenic. Unlocks Fuchsine making, Magenta dyeing.
# Picric Acid (1849)

Nitrate carbolic acid three times: a yellow silk dye, and later Lyddite. Needs Tar Distillation, Mineral Acids, Prussian Blue. Samples: 4 Phenol, 4 Nitric Acid. Unlocks Picric acid making, Yellow dyeing.
# Alizarin (1869)

Madder red from anthracene in a pressure vessel: the end of the madder fields (Graebe, Liebermann, Caro). Needs Tar Distillation, Prussian Blue, Steam Engine. Samples: 4 Anthracene, 4 Sodium Hydroxide. Unlocks Autoclave, Alizarin fusion, Red dyeing.
# Antiseptic Surgery (1867)
Carbolic acid on wounds, hands and instruments: carbolic soap cures an early Infection (Lister). Needs Tar Distillation, Hard Soap. Samples: 4 Phenol, 4 Hard Soap. Unlocks Carbolic Soap.
# Anaesthesia (1846)
Ether on a cloth puts a patient to sleep: a cure for a zombie villager takes half as long (Morton). Needs Sweet Oil of Vitriol. Samples: 4 Diethyl Ether, 2 White Wool. Unlocks Ether Anaesthetic.
# Dynamite (1867)

Nitroglycerin soaked into diatomite is safe to handle: Mining Charges break a 5 by 5 by 5 block of rock and keep every block (Nobel). Needs Soap Boiling, Mineral Acids, Lead Chamber Process. Samples: 4 Glycerol, 4 Nitric Acid. Unlocks Nitroglycerin making, Dynamite, Mining Charge.
# Cordite (1889)

Nitroglycerin and guncotton in cords: Cordite Cartridges hit 25% harder from the Breech-Loading Rifle and make no smoke (Abel and Dewar). Needs Dynamite, Smokeless Powder. Samples: 2 Nitroglycerin, 4 Smokeless Powder. Unlocks Cordite making, Cordite Cartridge.
# Aspirin (1897)

Salicylic acid from phenol in the Autoclave, then acetylated: aspirin eases nausea and fatigue and cures an early Infection (Kolbe, Hoffmann). Needs Tar Distillation, Alizarin. Samples: 4 Phenol, 4 Acetic Acid. Unlocks Kolbe schmitt, Aspirin making, Salicin oxidation.
# Bordeaux Mixture (1885)

Copper vitriol and lime sprayed on vines stops mildew: sprayed crops never wash out or wilt in the dark, and berry bushes stop scratching (Millardet). Needs Acid Digestion, Lime Burning. Samples: 4 Copper Ingot, 4 Calcium Oxide. Unlocks Copper vitriol, Bordeaux Mixture.
# Insect Powder (1840)

Dried Dalmatian daisies ground to powder: an Insect Spray that kills spiders, silverfish and endermites (and bees). Needs Oil Pressing. Samples: 8 Oxeye Daisy, 2 Spider Eye. Unlocks Pyrethrum grinding, Insect Spray.
# Vacuum Distillation (1880)

A pump on a still lowers the boiling points: a Vacuum Pump makes a still, kettle or crystallizer work 100 °C cooler. Needs Steam Engine, Tar Distillation. Samples: 8 Glass, 2 Mercury. Unlocks vacuum pump, Vacuum Pump.
# Rock Drill (1871)

Compressed air drove the drills that cut the Mont Cenis tunnel (Sommeiller 1861; Ingersoll 1871): the Air Compressor fills cylinders and the Pneumatic Rock Drill mines one block, a 1x3 tunnel or 3x3. Needs Gas Compression, Tungsten Steel. Samples: 2 Tungsten Steel Ingot, 2 Piston. Unlocks Air Compressor, Air compression, Pneumatic Rock Drill, Tungsten Steel Drill Bit.
# Lead-Acid Battery (1859)

Plante's lead plates in sulfuric acid store charge you can carry: a Lead-Acid Battery Pack holds 1,500 kJ and fills on a Charging Bench joined to the wire. Needs Dynamo. Samples: 8 Lead, 2 Sulfuric Acid. Unlocks Lead-Acid Battery Pack, Charging Bench.
# Diamond Core Drill (1863)

Leschot's drill with a crown of diamonds brings up a whole core of rock: the Atlas gains an ore layer from your cores and the ores you mine. Needs Geological Map, Bessemer Converter. Samples: 1 Diamond, 8 Steel Ingot. Unlocks Core Drill, Ores.
# Mapping Radioactivity (1898)

The Curies hunted uranium minerals with an electroscope: every reading you take is marked on the Atlas's radiation layer. Needs Radioactivity, Geological Map. Samples: 4 Raw Pitchblende, 8 Paper. Unlocks Radiation.
# Thin Sections (1858)

Sorby grinds rock to slices thin enough to see through under a microscope: the Compendium shows the minerals each rock is made of. Needs Theory of the Earth, Spectroscopy. Samples: 8 Glass, 8 Paper, 4 Diorite. Unlocks Petrography.
# Cold Greenhouse (1876)

Linde's refrigerating machine (1876) keeps a glasshouse cold: arctic and alpine plants grow anywhere; ice will do while it lasts. Needs Heated Greenhouse, Dynamo. Samples: 8 Packed Ice, 8 Copper Ingot. Unlocks Greenhouse Cooler.
# Alkaloids (1819)

Pelletier and Caventou drew emetine and quinine out of plants with acid water; Runge found caffeine (1819). Needs Acid Digestion. Samples: 4 Sulfuric Acid, 8 Poppy. Unlocks Caffeine extraction, Capsaicin extraction, Emetine extraction, Pilocarpine extraction.
# Mendel's Laws (1866)

Mendel counted his peas: each trait is two factors, one from each parent. The Seed Lens shows the genes themselves. Needs Plant Hybridization. Samples: 16 Beans, 8 Paper. Unlocks Genotype, Crossing Notebook.
# Silage (1877)
Goffart packed green maize in a pit and it kept all winter: the Silo turns maize, sorghum and alfalfa into silage. Needs Animal Husbandry. Samples: 16 Maize, 16 Alfalfa. Unlocks Silo.
# Nitrogen Fixation (1888)

Hellriegel and Wilfarth show that bacteria in the root nodules of legumes take nitrogen from the air: Inoculant gives a legume its rhizobia. Needs Crop Rotation. Samples: 16 Soybeans, 8 Dirt. Unlocks Inoculant.
# Rubber Belt Conveyor (1891)

Thomas Robins' rubber-covered belt carries coal and ore for miles (1891): the faster Rubber Belt, the Steel Hopper to keep up with it, and the Belt Sorter that turns chosen items aside. Needs Automatic Mill, Vulcanization. Samples: 4 Vulcanized Rubber, 4 Steel Ingot. Unlocks Rubber Belt, Steel Hopper, Belt Sorter.
# On the Origin of Species (1859)
Darwin's finches and pigeons: species change by natural selection. The Animal Compendium tells each animal's story. Needs Species Plantarum. Samples: 8 Paper, 4 Feather. Unlocks Evolution.
# Antivenom (1895)
Calmette raises horse serum against snake venom: venom, salt and a bottle make Antivenom, which cures poison. Needs Alkaloids. Samples: 4 Glass Bottle, 4 Spider Eye. Unlocks Antivenom.

text: Amounts are per 100 units of feed.
# Huntsman Crucible Furnace
- Tungsten steel: 100 Iron + 10.1 Tungsten (reagent) -> 110.1 Tungsten Steel Ingot. 1500 to 1650 °C.
# Bessemer Converter
- Bessemer decarburization: 100 Carbon -> nothing kept; vents Carbon Monoxide. 1200 to 1700 °C.
- Manganese steel: 100 Iron + 14.2 Manganese (reagent) -> 114.2 Manganese Steel Ingot. 1450 to 1700 °C.
- Bessemer steel: 100 Iron -> 100 Steel Ingot. 1450 to 1700 °C.
# Charcoal Blast Furnace
- Pyrolusite reduction: 100 Manganese Dioxide + 27.63 carbon -> 63.19 Manganese; vents Carbon Monoxide. 1200 to 1550 °C.

text: # University Research Institute
Research station for level 5, the age of steel alloys and rare earths.

@grid periodic_elements:university_laboratory*1|minecraft:glass,periodic_elements:aluminium,minecraft:glass/periodic_elements:copper_wire,periodic_elements:industrial_laboratory,periodic_elements:copper_wire/periodic_elements:steel_ingot,periodic_elements:steel_ingot,periodic_elements:steel_ingot
# Projects (★ = key)
# ★ Electric Arc Furnace (1900)

Strike an arc between graphite electrodes: heat no fuel can give, for silicon and ferroalloys (Heroult 1900). Needs Dynamo, Hall-Heroult Process. Samples: 16 Copper Wire, 8 Coke. Unlocks Electric Arc Furnace, Silica reduction, Chromite smelting.
# ★ Haber-Bosch Process (1909)

Bread from air: ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen at 200 atmospheres (Haber 1909, Bosch 1913). Needs Liquid Air, Chlor-Alkali Process. Samples: 4 Nitrogen, 4 Hydrogen. Unlocks High-Pressure Reactor, Ammonia synthesis.
# ★ Froth Flotation (1905)

Pine oil and bubbles float sulfide grains away from the rock: ores too poor to smelt become worth mining. Needs Electrolytic Refining, Mond Process. Samples: 8 Raw Molybdenite, 4 Spruce Log. Unlocks Flotation Cell, Molybdenite flotation, Rhenium flotation.
# ★ Stainless Steel (1913)
Steel with an eighth chromium does not rust (Brearley 1913). Needs Electric Arc Furnace. Samples: 4 Ferrochrome, 8 Iron Ingot. Unlocks Stainless steel, Stainless Steel Tools, Stainless Steel Armor.
# ★ Rare Earths (1885)

Crack monazite in acid and crystallize its salts again and again until the rare earths part (Auer von Welsbach). Needs Spectroscopy, Thorium. Samples: 16 Heavy Mineral Concentrate, 4 Sulfuric Acid. Unlocks Fractional Crystallizer, Monazite cracking, Cerium separation, Cerium reduction.
# ★ Crystal Bar Process (1925)

Grow pure zirconium on a hot wire from its iodide vapour (van Arkel and de Boer 1925). Needs Electric Arc Furnace, Iodine. Samples: 8 Heavy Mineral Concentrate, 2 Iodine. Unlocks Van Arkel Reactor, Zircon fusion, Zirconia reduction, Zirconium crystal bar.
# Ostwald Process (1902)
Burn ammonia on a platinum-rhodium gauze: nitric acid without saltpetre. Needs Haber-Bosch Process, Platinum Group Metals. Samples: 4 Ammonia, 1 Rhodium. Unlocks Ostwald Converter, Ammonia oxidation.
# Chromium (1898)

Pure chromium from chromite: roast with soda and burn the green oxide with aluminium (Goldschmidt 1898). Needs Electric Arc Furnace, Vanadium. Samples: 8 Raw Chromite, 4 Aluminium. Unlocks Chromite roasting, Chromate reduction, Chromium thermite.
# Molybdenum (1781)

Roast molybdenite to its white oxide and reduce it with hydrogen (Hjelm 1781). Needs Froth Flotation, Pneumatic Chemistry. Samples: 4 Molybdenite Concentrate, 2 Hydrogen. Unlocks Molybdenite roasting, Molybdenum reduction.
# Rhenium (1925)

The last stable element found, in the flue of a molybdenite roaster (Noddack, Tacke and Berg 1925). Needs Molybdenum, Spectroscopy. Samples: 8 Molybdenite Concentrate. Unlocks Rhenium roasting, Rhenium reduction.
# High-Speed Steel (1900)

Tool steel hardened from near melting cuts while red hot (Taylor and White 1900). Needs Molybdenum, Tungsten Steel, Electric Arc Furnace. Samples: 4 Tungsten Steel Ingot, 2 Molybdenum. Unlocks High speed steel, High Speed Steel Tools.
# Cemented Carbide (1926)

Tungsten carbide grains sintered in cobalt: wie Diamant (Widia 1926). Needs High-Speed Steel, Cobalt. Samples: 4 Tungsten, 2 Cobalt. Unlocks Sintering Furnace, Carbide sintering, Cemented Carbide Tools.
# Beryllium Copper (1926)

Copper with 2% beryllium is as hard as steel and never sparks: tools for mines and powder works. Needs Beryllium, Electrolytic Refining. Samples: 2 Beryllium, 8 Copper Ingot. Unlocks Beryllium copper, Beryllium Copper Tools.
# Niobium (1866)

Niobium parted from tantalum by crystallizing their fluoride salts (Marignac 1866). Needs Fluorine, Electric Arc Furnace. Samples: 8 Raw Coltan, 4 Hydrogen Fluoride. Unlocks Columbite digestion, Niobium reduction.
# Tantalum (1903)
Ductile tantalum melted in the arc for lamp filaments (von Bolton 1903). Needs Niobium. Samples: 8 Raw Coltan, 1 Niobium. Unlocks Tantalite digestion, Tantalum reduction.
# Lanthanum (1839)
"Hidden": the earth hiding in ceria (Mosander 1839). Needs Rare Earths. Samples: 8 Rare Earth Sulfates. Unlocks Lanthanum separation, Lanthanum reduction.
# Praseodymium and Neodymium (1885)

Didymium is two elements: green and pink salts after a hundred crystallizations (Auer von Welsbach 1885). Needs Lanthanum. Samples: 16 Rare Earth Sulfates. Unlocks Praseodymium separation, Neodymium separation, Praseodymium reduction, Neodymium reduction.
# Hafnium (1923)

X-ray lines showed a new element in every zircon; its fluoride crystallizes apart (Coster and Hevesy 1923). Needs Crystal Bar Process, Spectroscopy. Samples: 8 Crude Zirconia, 4 Hydrogen Fluoride. Unlocks Hafnium separation, Hafnium reduction, Hafnium crystal bar.
# Protactinium (1918)
The mother of actinium, found in pitchblende residue (Hahn and Meitner 1918). Needs Radium. Samples: 4 Pitchblende Residue. Unlocks Residue protactinium, Protactinium separation.
# Francium (1939)

Element 87: a branch in actinium's decay, carried by caesium salt, gone within the hour (Perey 1939). Needs Actinium, Caesium and Rubidium. Samples: 1 Actinium, 4 Caesium Chloride. Unlocks Francium precipitation.
# Geiger Counter (1928)
A gas tube that clicks for every ray: read radiation as you walk (Geiger and Muller 1928). Needs Radioactivity, Dynamo. Samples: 8 Copper Wire, 4 Glass. Unlocks Geiger Counter.
# ★ Thermal Cracking (1913)

Burton's pressure stills crack heavy oil into gasoline; the cracked gas is rich in ethylene. Needs Oil Refining, Electric Arc Furnace. Samples: 8 Diesel, 8 Steel Ingot. Unlocks Cracking Unit, Diesel cracking.
# Coal Liquefaction (1913)

Bergius hydrogenated powdered coal at 200 atmospheres into petrol and middle oil (Nobel Prize 1931). Needs Haber-Bosch Process, Oil Refining. Samples: 16 Coal, 4 Hydrogen. Unlocks Coal hydrogenation, Coal deoxygenation, Coal desulfurization.
# Liquid-Fuel Rocket (1926)

Goddard flew a rocket on liquid fuel and liquid oxygen (1926): kerosene rockets push an elytra like three charges of gunpowder. Needs Oil Refining, Liquid Air. Samples: 4 Kerosene, 4 Oxygen. Unlocks Kerosene Rocket.

Vinyl chloride from ethylene and chlorine, polymerised and made flexible by Semon (1926); PVC-sleeved cable carries current four times as far as bare wire. Needs Thermal Cracking, Chlor-Alkali Process. Samples: 4 Ethylene, 4 Chlorine. Unlocks Pvc synthesis, Insulated Cable.
# ★ Polyethylene (1933)

ICI found that ethylene at 1500 atmospheres with a trace of oxygen becomes a waxy white solid (1933): first radar cable, then everything. Needs Thermal Cracking, Haber-Bosch Process. Samples: 8 Ethylene. Unlocks Polyethylene polymerization.
# Catalyst Beds (1909)

Mittasch tests thousands of catalysts for Haber's ammonia: a Catalyst Bed doubles the rate of reactions over iron, nickel, platinum or vanadium oxide. Needs Haber-Bosch Process, Contact Process. Samples: 2 Platinum, 4 Nickel. Unlocks Catalyst Bed, catalyst bed.
# Calcium Carbide (1892)

Quicklime and coke fused in the arc make carbide; water on carbide gives acetylene, the flame of the miner's Carbide Lamp (Willson 1892). Needs Electric Arc Furnace, Lime Burning. Samples: 8 Calcium Oxide, 8 Coke. Unlocks Carbide smelting, Acetylene generation, Carbide Lamp.
# Nitrolime (1898)

Hot carbide takes up nitrogen: calcium cyanamide, the first fertilizer made from the air (Frank and Caro 1898). Needs Calcium Carbide, Liquid Air. Samples: 4 Calcium Carbide, 4 Nitrogen. Unlocks Cyanamide making.
# Oxy-Acetylene Welding (1903)

Acetylene burnt in pure oxygen is hot enough to melt steel: a Welding Torch mends metal tools and armour with ingots and no experience (Fouche and Picard 1903). Needs Calcium Carbide, Gas Compression. Samples: 4 Acetylene, 4 Oxygen. Unlocks Welding Torch.
# Formaldehyde (1889)

Wood spirit and air over red-hot silver give formaldehyde, the other half of the first plastics (Hofmann 1867; made by the tonne from 1889). Needs Alembic Distillation, Ostwald Process. Samples: 4 Methanol, 1 Silver. Unlocks Formaldehyde making.
# Bakelite (1907)

Phenol and formaldehyde under pressure set into Bakelite: hard, dark, and it takes a polish; coloured Bakelite blocks and Bakelite-cased Geiger counters (Baekeland 1907). Needs Formaldehyde, Alizarin. Samples: 4 Phenol, 4 Formaldehyde. Unlocks Bakelite making, Bakelite Blocks, Geiger Counter Bakelite.
# Urea Synthesis (1922)
Ammonia and carbon dioxide at 150 atmospheres become urea, the richest nitrogen fertilizer (Bosch and Meiser 1922). Needs Haber-Bosch Process. Samples: 4 Ammonia, 4 Calcite. Unlocks Urea synthesis.
# Prilled Fertilizer (1935)

Melt dropped down a tall tower freezes into hard round prills that flow and keep: ammonium nitrate, and NPK prills that make crops grow twice as fast. Needs Urea Synthesis, Ostwald Process, Superphosphate. Samples: 4 Urea, 4 Superphosphate. Unlocks Prilling Tower, An neutralizing, Npk prilling, PK Blend, NPK Prills.

Toluene nitrated three times: TNT is safe to melt and pour, and a Demolition Charge breaks even obsidian (Wilbrand 1863; army filling from 1902). Needs Dynamite, Tar Distillation. Samples: 4 Toluene, 4 Nitric Acid. Unlocks Tnt making, Demolition Charge, Tnt From Trinitrotoluene.
# Acetone Fermentation (1916)

Weizmann's bacterium turns the starch of grain or potatoes into acetone and butanol: the acetone for wartime cordite (1916). Needs Mashing, Cordite. Samples: 8 Potato, 2 Calcite. Unlocks Abe fermentation.
# Neoprene (1931)

Chloroprene rubber from acetylene: it shrugs off oil and cold; a neoprene Wetsuit swims like a dolphin and never freezes (Carothers 1931). Needs Calcium Carbide, Chlor-Alkali Process. Samples: 4 Acetylene, 4 Hydrochloric Acid. Unlocks Neoprene making, Wetsuit.
# Buna Rubber (1929)

Synthetic rubber from alcohol and benzene, no jungle needed: Rubber Wheels, and a Conveyor Belt that empties a machine four items at a time (Lebedev 1926, IG Farben 1929). Needs Vulcanization, Thermal Cracking. Samples: 4 Ethanol, 4 Benzene. Unlocks Lebedev butadiene, Styrene making, Buna polymerization, Conveyor Belt, conveyor belt, Rubber Wheels Buna.
# Sulfa Drugs (1935)

A red dye cured streptococcus in mice; its active half, sulfanilamide, cures Infection and even sepsis (Domagk 1932, Trefouel 1935). Needs Aniline, Gas Liquor. Samples: 4 Aniline, 4 Ammonium Sulfate. Unlocks Sulfanilamide making.
# Biodiesel (1937)

Plant oil or tallow with methanol and lye gives methyl esters that run a Diesel Generator: fuel from the farm (Chavanne 1937). Needs Soap Boiling, Diesel Engine, Alembic Distillation. Samples: 4 Vegetable Oil, 4 Methanol. Unlocks Biodiesel tallow, Biodiesel oil.
# Rotary Hammer (1932)

An electric motor turns and hammers the bit at once (Bosch 1932): the Rotary Hammer runs on a battery pack and never slows you. Needs Rock Drill, Lead-Acid Battery, High-Speed Steel. Samples: 2 High-Speed Steel Ingot, 4 Copper Wire. Unlocks Electric Rotary Hammer, High-Speed Steel Drill Bit, Cemented Carbide Drill Bit.
# Chainsaw (1926)

A cutting chain driven round a bar (Stihl 1926): the Chainsaw fells a whole tree, up to 128 logs, on battery power. Needs Lead-Acid Battery, Electric Motor. Samples: 4 Steel Ingot, 16 Oak Log. Unlocks Chainsaw.
# Magnetic and Seismic Prospecting (1921)

Magnetometers and the first seismic reflection surveys see ore bodies from the surface: an anomaly layer, without naming the ore. Needs Diamond Core Drill, Dynamo. Samples: 8 Copper Wire, 1 Compass. Unlocks Prospecting Magnetometer, Anomalies.
# Geiger Survey (1928)
Carry a Geiger counter and the radiation where you walk is logged on the Atlas by itself. Needs Geiger Counter, Mapping Radioactivity. Samples: 8 Raw Pitchblende, 8 Paper. Unlocks Geiger Log.
# Radio Direction Finding (c. 1910)

Radio beacons let ships and aircraft fix their place: a Radio Transmitter shares your Atlas markers with every player who knows radio within 512 blocks. Needs Dynamo, Portolan Charts. Samples: 16 Copper Wire, 8 Redstone. Unlocks Radio Transmitter, Radio.
# X-ray Diffraction (1913)

The Braggs bounce X-rays off crystals and read the spacing of their atoms: the Compendium shows each mineral's formula and crystal system. Needs Thin Sections, Geiger Counter. Samples: 8 Quartz, 4 Amethyst Shard, 8 Paper. Unlocks Crystals.
# Vitamins (1928)

Szent-Györgyi drew hexuronic acid out of paprika (1928): vitamin C, the cure for scurvy, and with the same methods arbutin from bearberry. Needs Alkaloids. Samples: 4 Citric Acid, 8 Apple. Unlocks Vitamin C extraction, Arbutin extraction.
# Hybrid Maize (1922)
Shull and Jones cross inbred lines of maize: the first generation grows with hybrid vigour. The Seed Lens marks hybrids and pure lines. Needs Mendel's Laws. Samples: 32 Maize Kernels. Unlocks Hybrid.
# Balanced Feed (1925)
Feed with energy, protein, minerals and salt in the right shares: animals grow and breed faster on it. Needs Animal Husbandry. Samples: 16 Oats, 4 Protein Meal. Unlocks Balanced Feed.
# X-ray Mutagenesis (1928)

Stadler X-rays barley seeds and the plants come out changed: the Seed Irradiator makes mutations twenty times as common. Needs Mendel's Laws, X-ray Diffraction. Samples: 32 Wheat Seeds, 4 Lead. Unlocks Seed Irradiator.
# Moving Assembly Line (1913)

Ford's line brings the work to the worker on rollers and chains (1913): the Roller Conveyor and the Stainless Steel Hopper. Needs Rubber Belt Conveyor, Stainless Steel. Samples: 4 Stainless Steel Ingot, 8 Redstone. Unlocks Roller Conveyor, Stainless Steel Hopper.
# Electric Cap Lamp (1911)

Edison's miner's lamp: a tungsten bulb on the helmet fed by the battery pack, light 15 that follows you. Needs Lead-Acid Battery, Tungsten Steel. Samples: 2 Tungsten, 2 Glass. Unlocks Electric Cap Lamp.
# Sodium Street Lighting (1932)

Low-pressure sodium vapour shines yellow at 589 nm: a Sodium Lamp on a post keeps monsters from spawning within 24 blocks. Needs Neon, Krypton and Xenon, Dynamo. Samples: 4 Sodium, 2 Neon. Unlocks Sodium Lamp.
# Hirudin (1904)
The anticoagulant of the medicinal leech, drawn out in a Digestion Vat. Needs Vitamins. Samples: 4 Glass Bottle, 4 Slime Ball. Unlocks Hirudin extraction.
# Galalith (1897)

Casein from skim milk hardened in formalin: galalith, the milk-stone of buttons and pens (Spitteler and Krische 1897). Needs Formaldehyde. Samples: 2 Milk Bucket, 2 Formaldehyde. Unlocks Galalith making.
# Vitamin D (1922)
Cod and shark liver oil cures rickets (McCollum 1922): vitamin D3 drawn out in a Digestion Vat. Needs Vitamins. Samples: 8 Cod, 4 Glass Bottle. Unlocks Vitamin D extraction.

# Projects (★ = key)
# ★ Kroll Process (1940)

Chlorinate the black sand, then strip the chlorine with magnesium under argon: titanium by the tonne (Kroll 1940). Needs Electric Arc Furnace, Alkaline Earth Metals. Samples: 16 Heavy Mineral Concentrate, 4 Magnesium. Unlocks Chlorinator, Kroll Reactor, Ilmenite chlorination, Rutile chlorination, Kroll reduction.
# ★ Ion Exchange (1947)

Resin columns part in days the rare earths a century of crystallizing could not (Spedding 1947). Needs Rare Earths, Praseodymium and Neodymium. Samples: 16 Heavy Mineral Concentrate, 4 Hydrochloric Acid. Unlocks Ion-Exchange Column, Xenotime leaching, Yttrium exchange, Yttrium reduction.
# ★ Single Crystals (1950)

Grow one flawless crystal from the melt and sweep it clean: the stuff of transistors (Teal, Pfann). Needs Electric Arc Furnace, Germanium. Samples: 4 Silicon, 1 Germanium. Unlocks Crystal Puller, Zone Refiner, Silicon crystal, Germanium crystal.
# ★ Synthetic Diamond (1954)

Graphite in molten nickel squeezed to 50000 atmospheres becomes diamond (General Electric 1954). Needs Cemented Carbide, Mond Process. Samples: 8 Cemented Carbide, 4 Nickel. Unlocks Diamond Press, Diamond synthesis, Synthetic Diamond Tools.
# ★ Uranium Metal (1942)

Green salt reduced by magnesium in a sealed bomb: uranium for the first reactor (Ames 1942). Needs Fluorine, Kroll Process. Samples: 8 Uranium Oxide, 4 Magnesium. Unlocks Uranium hydrofluorination, Uranium reduction.
# Titanium Alloy (1954)

Titanium with 6% aluminium and 4% vanadium: netherite's strength, half the weight. Needs Kroll Process, Vanadium. Samples: 4 Titanium, 2 Vanadium. Unlocks Aluminium vanadium alloy, Titanium alloy, Titanium Alloy Tools, Titanium Alloy Armor.
# Scandium (1937)
Mendeleev's eka-boron, first made as metal in 1937 (Fischer). Needs Ion Exchange. Samples: 4 Heavy Rare Earth Chlorides. Unlocks Scandium exchange, Scandium reduction.
# Samarium and Europium (1901)

Samarium from samarskite (Lecoq 1879) and europium split from it (Demarcay 1901). Needs Ion Exchange. Samples: 4 Heavy Rare Earth Chlorides. Unlocks Samarium exchange, Europium exchange, Samarium reduction, Europium reduction.
# Gadolinium and Terbium (1886)

Gadolinium (Marignac 1880) and terbium, the second earth of Ytterby. Needs Ion Exchange. Samples: 4 Heavy Rare Earth Chlorides. Unlocks Gadolinium exchange, Terbium exchange, Gadolinium reduction, Terbium reduction.
# Dysprosium and Holmium (1886)

Dysprosium, "hard to get at" (Lecoq 1886), and holmium for Stockholm (Cleve 1878). Needs Ion Exchange. Samples: 4 Heavy Rare Earth Chlorides. Unlocks Dysprosium exchange, Holmium exchange, Dysprosium reduction, Holmium reduction.
# Erbium and Thulium (1879)
Pink erbium and thulium for Thule (Cleve 1879). Needs Ion Exchange. Samples: 4 Heavy Rare Earth Chlorides. Unlocks Erbium exchange, Thulium exchange, Erbium reduction, Thulium reduction.
# Ytterbium and Lutetium (1907)

The last rare earth found in nature, split from ytterbium (Urbain 1907). Needs Ion Exchange. Samples: 4 Heavy Rare Earth Chlorides. Unlocks Ytterbium exchange, Lutetium exchange, Ytterbium reduction, Lutetium reduction.
# Solar Cell (1954)
A silicon wafer turns sunlight straight into current (Bell Labs 1954). Needs Single Crystals, Dynamo. Samples: 4 Silicon Wafer, 8 Copper Wire. Unlocks Solar Panel.
# ★ Isotope Separation (1945)

Uranium-235 is 0.7% of uranium and chemically the same: only its lighter weight can part it (Oak Ridge 1945). Needs Uranium Metal. Samples: 8 Uranium Tetrafluoride, 8 Nickel. Unlocks Enrichment Cascade, Diffuser Stage, Uranium hexafluoride synthesis, Uranium enrichment, Depleted uranium reduction.
# ★ Nuclear Reactor (1942)

A pile of uranium and graphite went critical under a Chicago stand: neutrons split uranium faster than they escape (Fermi 1942). Needs Isotope Separation, Crystal Bar Process. Samples: 4 Uranium, 16 Coke, 2 Cadmium. Unlocks Nuclear Reactor, Graphite Block, Fuel Channel, Reactor Shielding, Fuel conversion, Fuel pellet sintering, Zircaloy.
# ★ Reprocessing (1954)

Behind lead glass, spent fuel is dissolved and its uranium and plutonium pulled out by solvent (PUREX, Savannah River 1954). Needs Nuclear Reactor. Samples: 1 Spent Fuel Rod, 8 Nitric Acid. Unlocks Hot Cell, Recovered uranium, Plutonium extraction, Plutonium reduction.
# Neptunium (1940)
The first element beyond uranium, made by neutrons on uranium (McMillan and Abelson 1940). Needs Reprocessing. Samples: 2 Spent Fuel Rod. Unlocks Neptunium extraction, Neptunium reduction.
# Technetium (1937)

The gap at 43 was filled by an element no ore holds: first from a cyclotron part, now by the kilogram from fission (Perrier and Segre 1937). Needs Reprocessing. Samples: 2 Spent Fuel Rod. Unlocks Technetium extraction.
# Promethium (1945)

The missing rare earth, found among the fission products of the Oak Ridge reactor (Marinsky, Glendenin and Coryell 1945). Needs Reprocessing, Ion Exchange. Samples: 2 Spent Fuel Rod. Unlocks Promethium extraction, Promethium reduction.
# Americium and Curium (1944)

Plutonium soaked in neutrons gives americium, and americium gives curium (Seaborg, James, Morgan and Ghiorso 1944). Needs Reprocessing. Samples: 2 Plutonium. Unlocks Americium extraction, Americium reduction, Curium extraction, Curium reduction.
# Cyclotron (1932)

Particles whirled in a magnet and kicked at every half turn reach millions of volts (Lawrence 1932): astatine was made in one (1940). Needs Isotope Separation. Samples: 16 Copper Wire, 4 Helium. Unlocks Cyclotron, Astatine synthesis.
# Berkelium and Californium (1950)

Alpha particles on americium and curium gave elements 97 and 98, named for Berkeley and California (1949-50). Needs Cyclotron, Americium and Curium. Samples: 2 Americium, 2 Curium. Unlocks Berkelium synthesis, Californium synthesis.
# Mendelevium (1955)

Einsteinium from the first hydrogen bomb's debris, bombarded in the cyclotron one atom at a time (Ghiorso 1955). Needs Berkelium and Californium. Samples: 2 Einsteinium Sample. Unlocks Mendelevium synthesis.
# Radioisotope Generator (1961)

Neptunium irradiated into plutonium-238, whose decay heat thermocouples turn into current for decades (Transit 4A 1961, Voyager 1977). Needs Neptunium, Nuclear Reactor. Samples: 1 Neptunium, 4 Lead. Unlocks Radioisotope Generator.
# Smoke Detector (1965)

A speck of americium ionises the air in a chamber; smoke stops the current and the alarm sounds (Duane Pearsall 1965). Needs Americium and Curium. Samples: 1 Americium Dioxide, 4 Redstone. Unlocks Smoke Detector.
# ★ Catalytic Reforming (1949)

Platforming: naphtha over platinum becomes high-octane gasoline, benzene and xylene, and gives up hydrogen (UOP 1949). Needs Thermal Cracking, Platinum Group Metals. Samples: 8 Naphtha, 1 Platinum. Unlocks Naphtha reforming.
# Nylon (1935)

Carothers' nylon 6-6 (DuPont 1935), the first fully synthetic fibre: stockings, rope and parachutes. Needs Catalytic Reforming, Haber-Bosch Process. Samples: 4 Benzene, 4 Ammonia. Unlocks Nylon synthesis, Parachute, Nylon String.
# Heavy Water (1934)

Norsk Hydro's heavy water slows neutrons without catching them, so natural uranium can sustain a chain reaction (the Canadian CANDU reactors). Needs Isotope Separation. Samples: 8 Uranium. Unlocks Heavy water enrichment, Natural Uranium Fuel Rod.
# Styrene and Polystyrene (1941)

Styrene joins into clear, light polystyrene; blown with gas it is foam: Foam Lagging for cool machines and Insulation that keeps ice from melting (Dow 1941). Needs Buna Rubber, Polyethylene. Samples: 4 Styrene, 2 Methane. Unlocks Polystyrene making, Foam Lagging, foam lagging, Insulation.
# ★ Penicillin (1943)

Fleming's mould grown in deep, stirred tanks of sterile air: penicillin cures Infection, guards against it for 20 minutes, and with Weakness cures a zombie villager (1928, 1943). Needs Sulfa Drugs, Mashing, Electric Motor. Samples: 4 Melon Slice, 4 Glucose. Unlocks Deep-Tank Fermenter, Penicillin fermentation, Sterile Air Filter, sterile air filter.
# Streptomycin (1943)

An antibiotic from a soil bacterium, the first to cure tuberculosis: it cures Infection and guards against it for 20 minutes (Schatz and Waksman 1943). Needs Penicillin. Samples: 4 Dirt, 4 Protein Meal. Unlocks Streptomycin fermentation.

An insecticide that lasts: a DDT Duster leaves ground that kills insects for three days, and the chickens near it lay half as often (Muller 1939; Silent Spring 1962). Needs Insect Powder, Chlor-Alkali Process, Tar Distillation. Samples: 4 Benzene, 4 Chlorine. Unlocks Ddt making, DDT Duster.
# Weed Killer (1945)

A plant hormone that kills broad-leaved weeds and spares grass and grain: Weed Killer clears flowers, ferns, vines and leaves (1945). Needs DDT, Tar Distillation. Samples: 4 Phenol, 4 Chlorine. Unlocks Two four d making, Weed Killer.
# Atrazine (1958)

Sprayed before anything grows: Pre-Emergent stops grass and mycelium spreading onto the ground for ten days (Geigy 1958). Needs Weed Killer, Urea Synthesis. Samples: 4 Ammonia, 4 Chlorine. Unlocks Atrazine making, Pre-Emergent.
# Plastic Explosive (1943)

RDX from hexamine, kneaded with oil: a Shaped Charge with a copper liner bores a tunnel sixteen blocks deep (Henning 1898; Munroe effect). Needs TNT, Formaldehyde. Samples: 4 Formaldehyde, 4 Nitric Acid. Unlocks Hexamine making, Rdx making, Shaped Charge.

Fertilizer prills soaked in diesel: the cheapest blasting agent; an ANFO Charge breaks a 9x9x9 cube for the quarry (1955). Needs Prilled Fertilizer, Oil Refining. Samples: 8 Ammonium Nitrate, 2 Diesel. Unlocks ANFO Charge.
# Radiation Countermeasures (1960)

Potassium iodide tablets keep radioiodine out of the body, and Prussian blue capsules bind radiocaesium: each cuts the dose from fission products for a day. Needs Reprocessing, Prussian Blue, Iodine. Samples: 8 Dried Kelp, 4 Prussian Blue. Unlocks Iodide making, Prussian Blue Capsule.
# Heavy Mining Drill (1960)

Diamond core drilling: the Heavy Mining Drill adds a 5x5 head and a vein mode that follows one ore up to 32 blocks. Needs Rotary Hammer, Synthetic Diamond, Titanium Alloy. Samples: 2 Synthetic Diamond, 2 Titanium Alloy Ingot. Unlocks Heavy Mining Drill, Diamond Drill Bit.
# The Red List (1964)

The IUCN begins listing species at risk of extinction: the Compendium shows how threatened each tree is in the wild. Needs Geography of Plants, Penicillin. Samples: 16 Paper, 4 Book. Unlocks Conservation.
# Radar (1940)

Radio echoes off aircraft won the Battle of Britain: a Radar Station shows creatures and players within 96 blocks on the Atlas, and a Handheld Radar gives you a minimap. Needs Radio Direction Finding, Single Crystals. Samples: 16 Copper Wire, 1 Germanium Crystal. Unlocks Radar Station, Handheld Radar, Radar, Minimap.
# Airborne Gamma Spectrometry (c. 1950)

A sodium iodide crystal tells the gamma rays of uranium, thorium and caesium apart: the Atlas splits radiation by isotope, and reads the ground from the air. Needs Geiger Survey, Single Crystals. Samples: 4 Iodine, 1 Thallium. Unlocks Isotopes.
# Food Antioxidants (1943)

Fat kept from going rancid with a pinch of NDGA from the creosote bush (1943), until safer antioxidants replaced it. Needs Alkaloids, Ion Exchange. Samples: 4 Vegetable Oil, 4 Tallow. Unlocks NDGA extraction.
# DNA Double Helix (1953)

Franklin's X-ray picture, Watson and Crick's model: genes are written in DNA. The Seed Lens shows every trait, and the stature gene of wheat and rice. Needs Mendel's Laws, X-ray Diffraction. Samples: 16 Paper, 8 Soybeans. Unlocks Dna.
# Gamma Garden (1960)

A cobalt-60 source in a field of crops (Japan 1960): seeds of the plants around it mutate twenty times as often. Needs X-ray Mutagenesis, Cyclotron, Heavy Water. Samples: 4 Cobalt, 8 Lead. Unlocks Gamma Garden, Cobalt 60 activation.
# Night Vision (1944)

A silver-oxygen-caesium photocathode turns faint infrared into a picture: Night Vision Goggles show the dark and outline monsters. Needs Caesium and Rubidium, Dynamo. Samples: 2 Caesium, 4 Glass. Unlocks Night Vision Goggles.
# Nylon Backpack (1950)
Light, tough nylon on an aluminium frame: a Nylon Backpack with 54 places. Needs Nylon. Samples: 8 Nylon, 2 Chest. Unlocks Nylon Backpack.
# Chitosan (1859)

Crab shells boiled in strong lye lose their acetyl groups: chitosan, for wound dressings and water filters (Rouget 1859). Needs Vitamins. Samples: 2 Nautilus Shell, 8 Bone Meal. Unlocks Chitosan making.
