text: # International Research Centre
Research station for level 7: chips, superconductors and the last elements.

@grid periodic_elements:international_research_centre*1|minecraft:glass,periodic_elements:titanium_alloy_ingot,minecraft:glass/periodic_elements:silicon_wafer,periodic_elements:national_laboratory,periodic_elements:silicon_wafer/periodic_elements:titanium_alloy_ingot,periodic_elements:titanium_alloy_ingot,periodic_elements:titanium_alloy_ingot
# Projects (★ = key)
# ★ Superconducting Magnets (1962)

Niobium-titanium wire cooled by liquid helium carries current with no loss: the magnets of every big accelerator and MRI scanner. Needs Kroll Process, Crystal Bar Process. Samples: 4 Niobium, 4 Titanium, 4 Helium. Unlocks Niobium titanium.
# ★ Integrated Circuit (1959)

A whole circuit printed on one chip of silicon (Kilby 1958, Noyce 1959): the start of the information age. Needs Single Crystals, Solar Cell. Samples: 4 Silicon Wafer, 1 Boron. Unlocks Chip Fab, Integrated circuit.
# Compound Semiconductors (1962)

Gallium arsenide gives off light where silicon cannot: the first visible LED and the semiconductor laser (Holonyak 1962). The Heavy-Ion Accelerator needs its wafers. Needs Integrated Circuit. Samples: 2 Gallium, 2 Arsenic. Unlocks Gallium arsenide.
# Electromagnetic Isotope Separation (1943)

Lawrence's calutrons bent uranium ions apart by mass at Oak Ridge; today they make rare isotopes such as calcium-48. Needs Isotope Separation, Superconducting Magnets. Samples: 8 Calcium. Unlocks Calutron, Calcium 48 separation.
# ★ Heavy-Ion Accelerator (1958)

Whole nuclei, not just helium, fired at heavy targets: elements 102 and 103 at Berkeley and Dubna (1958-66). Needs Superconducting Magnets, Integrated Circuit, Mendelevium. Samples: 4 Niobium-Titanium Wire, 4 Integrated Circuit, 1 Curium. Unlocks Heavy-Ion Accelerator, Nobelium synthesis, Lawrencium synthesis.
# Rutherfordium to Seaborgium (1974)

Carbon, nitrogen and oxygen beams on californium gave elements 104 to 106 (Ghiorso, Berkeley 1969-74). Needs Heavy-Ion Accelerator. Samples: 2 Californium Sample. Unlocks Rutherfordium synthesis, Dubnium synthesis, Seaborgium synthesis.
# Cold Fusion of Heavy Nuclei (1981)

Gentle collisions of medium nuclei with lead and bismuth gave elements 107 to 113, one atom a week (GSI 1981-96, RIKEN 2004). Needs Heavy-Ion Accelerator. Samples: 4 Bismuth, 4 Lead. Unlocks Bohrium synthesis, Hassium synthesis, Meitnerium synthesis, Darmstadtium synthesis, Roentgenium synthesis, Copernicium synthesis, Nihonium synthesis.
# Calcium-48 Hot Fusion (1999)

A calcium-48 beam on actinide targets reached the island of stability's shore: elements 114 to 118 (Oganessian, Dubna 1999-2010). Needs Heavy-Ion Accelerator, Electromagnetic Isotope Separation. Samples: 2 Calcium-48, 2 Plutonium. Unlocks Flerovium synthesis, Moscovium synthesis, Livermorium synthesis, Tennessine synthesis, Oganesson synthesis.
# Neodymium Magnets (1984)

Neodymium, iron and boron make the strongest magnets (Sagawa 1984): direct-drive wind turbines with no gearbox. Needs Praseodymium and Neodymium, Electric Arc Furnace. Samples: 2 Neodymium, 1 Boron. Unlocks Iron boron alloy, Neodymium magnet, Wind Turbine.
# Composite Armour (1965)

Ceramic tiles shatter the bullet and woven aramid catches it: boron carbide plates over titanium (Kwolek's Kevlar 1965). Needs Titanium Alloy, Catalytic Reforming. Samples: 2 Boron, 2 Titanium Alloy Ingot. Unlocks Boron carbide, Xylene oxidation, Ppd synthesis, Aramid polymerization.
# The Periodic Table Complete (2016)

IUPAC named the last four elements in 2016: the seventh row of the periodic table is full. Needs Rutherfordium to Seaborgium, Cold Fusion of Heavy Nuclei, Calcium-48 Hot Fusion. Samples: 1 Nihonium Detection Record, 1 Moscovium Detection Record, 1 Tennessine Detection Record, 1 Oganesson Detection Record.
# Lithium-Ion Battery (1991)

Lithium ions shuttle between a cobalt oxide cathode and a carbon anode (Goodenough 1980, Yoshino 1985, Sony 1991). Needs Integrated Circuit. Samples: 4 Lithium, 2 Cobalt. Unlocks Lithium-Ion Battery, Lithium cobalt oxide.
# Optical Fibre (1987)

Light in glass fibre amplified by erbium carries a world network (Kao 1966, Payne and Desurvire 1987). Needs Compound Semiconductors. Samples: 1 Erbium, 4 Quartz. Unlocks Optical fibre, Fibre Communicator.
# Element Analyzer (1997)

Curium-244 alpha particles and X-rays read every element in a rock: the APXS of the Mars rovers (Sojourner 1997). Needs Americium and Curium, Integrated Circuit. Samples: 1 Curium Oxide, 2 Silicon Wafer. Unlocks Element Analyzer.
# Calutron Enrichment (1944)

The Y-12 calutrons enriched the uranium of the first bomb; afterwards they enriched lithium-6, boron-10 and hundreds of other isotopes for science. Needs Electromagnetic Isotope Separation. Samples: 8 Uranium, 2 Lithium, 2 Boron. Unlocks Uranium 235 separation, Lithium 6 separation, Boron 10 separation, Enriched metal fuel.
# Boron Control Rods (1942)
Boron-10 swallows neutrons: control rods throttle a reactor so it stops burning fuel it has no room to store. Needs Calutron Enrichment. Samples: 4 Boron, 4 Steel Ingot. Unlocks Control rod pressing.
# Tritium (1934)

Lithium-6 in a reactor catches a neutron and splits into helium and tritium; tritium's soft beta light makes signs glow for decades with no power. Needs Calutron Enrichment, Nuclear Reactor. Samples: 4 Lithium. Unlocks Tritium Light.
# Glyphosate (1970)

A weed killer that kills every green plant: Field Clear spares only crops grown from tolerant seeds (Franz 1970). Needs Atrazine, Formaldehyde. Samples: 4 Formaldehyde, 4 Phosphoric Acid. Unlocks Glyphosate making, Field Clear.
# ★ Recombinant DNA (1973)

Genes cut and pasted into bacteria: the Bioreactor, a chip-run vessel for engineered microbes (Cohen and Boyer 1973). Needs Penicillin, Integrated Circuit. Samples: 2 Integrated Circuit, 8 Glucose. Unlocks Bioreactor.
# Cellulosic Ethanol (2005)
Enzymes break the cellulose of any plant to sugar: ethanol from logs, leaves and straw. Needs Recombinant DNA. Samples: 8 Oak Log, 4 Ethanol. Unlocks Cellulose fermentation.
# Tolerant Seeds (1996)

A bacterial gene makes wheat shrug off glyphosate: Tolerant Seeds survive Field Clear and grow a tenth faster. Needs Recombinant DNA, Glyphosate. Samples: 16 Wheat Seeds, 2 Glyphosate. Unlocks Tolerant Seeds.
# PLA Bioplastic (2001)

Plastic fermented from sugar that composts away: flower pots and item frames from PLA. Needs Recombinant DNA, Styrene and Polystyrene. Samples: 8 Glucose, 8 Sugar Cane. Unlocks Pla making, Pla Flower Pot, Pla Item Frame.
# mRNA Vaccine (2020)

Messenger RNA in a droplet of fat teaches the body its enemy: seven game days with no Infection (Kariko and Weissman; 2020). Needs Recombinant DNA, Streptomycin. Samples: 4 Protein Meal, 4 Vegetable Oil. Unlocks Vaccine making, mRNA Vaccine.
# Amifostine (1995)

A radioprotector from the Walter Reed programme: for an hour, radiation does half the harm (1959; approved 1995). Needs Recombinant DNA, Radiation Countermeasures. Samples: 4 Phosphoric Acid, 4 Ammonium Sulfate. Unlocks Amifostine making, Taxol extraction.
# Lithium-Ion Pack (1991)

Four times the charge of lead at half the weight: a Lithium-Ion Pack holds 6,000 kJ and the Heavy Mining Drill no longer slows you. Needs Heavy Mining Drill, Lithium-Ion Battery. Samples: 2 Lithium Cobalt Oxide, 1 Integrated Circuit. Unlocks Lithium-Ion Pack.
# Ore-Seeking Drill (1997)

The element analyzer built into the drill head: in vein mode, use the Heavy Mining Drill on an ore to read the whole vein before you dig. Needs Heavy Mining Drill, Element Analyzer. Samples: 2 Integrated Circuit, 8 Raw Iron. Unlocks Ore-Seeking Drill.
# Satellite and Tracking Station (1957)

Sputnik's beeps were heard all round the world: launch a satellite and a Tracking Station maps 512 blocks all round it each day, without going there. Needs Radar, Solar Cell. Samples: 4 Titanium Alloy Ingot, 4 Kerosene. Unlocks Satellite, Launch Pad, Tracking Station, Satellite.
# Multispectral Scanner (1972)

Landsat saw rocks and minerals in bands of light the eye cannot: your satellites note the rock and the ores near the surface of what they map. Needs Satellite and Tracking Station, Integrated Circuit. Samples: 2 Integrated Circuit, 2 Silicon Wafer. Unlocks Multispectral Scanner.
# Global Positioning System (1978)

Atomic clocks in orbit give anyone their place to a few metres: a GPS Receiver shows the minimap anywhere, marks where you die and routes you to your markers. Needs Satellite and Tracking Station, Integrated Circuit. Samples: 4 Integrated Circuit, 1 Caesium. Unlocks GPS Receiver, Global Positioning System.
# DNA Sequencing (1977)
Sanger reads DNA letter by letter: the DNA Sequencer shows the whole genome of a seed. Needs DNA Double Helix, Integrated Circuit. Samples: 2 Integrated Circuit, 8 Glucose. Unlocks DNA Sequencer.

Mullis copies a stretch of DNA a billion times by heating and cooling it: the Thermocycler tests seeds for a marker's genes and sorts them. Needs DNA Sequencing. Samples: 2 Integrated Circuit, 8 Glucose. Unlocks Thermocycler.
# Transgenesis (1987)

Sanford shoots gold beads coated with DNA into plant cells: the Gene Gun gives crops the Bt, EPSPS, golden rice and DREB genes. Needs Recombinant DNA, DNA Double Helix. Samples: 4 Gold Ingot, 4 Helium. Unlocks Gene Gun, Bt Gene, EPSPS Gene, Golden Rice Gene, DREB Gene.
# CRISPR (2012)

Charpentier and Doudna turn a bacterial defence into scissors for DNA: the CRISPR Kit rewrites one gene of a crop. Needs Transgenesis, PCR. Samples: 2 Integrated Circuit, 16 Glucose. Unlocks CRISPR Kit.
# White LED (1996)

Blue gallium nitride light (Nakamura 1993) under a yellow phosphor gives white: LED Lamps reach 40 blocks on little power, and the LED Spotlight Helmet lights where you look. Needs Compound Semiconductors. Samples: 4 Gallium, 4 Nitrogen. Unlocks LED Lamp, LED Spotlight Helmet.
# Exenatide (2005)
A peptide from Gila monster saliva becomes a diabetes medicine, made in the Bioreactor. Needs Recombinant DNA. Samples: 4 Glass Bottle, 4 Egg. Unlocks Exenatide making.
# LAL Test (1977)

Horseshoe crab blood clots at a trace of bacterial endotoxin: every injectable medicine is tested with it (Bang and Levin). Needs Recombinant DNA. Samples: 4 Glass Bottle, 4 Copper Ingot. Unlocks LAL extraction.
# Green Fluorescent Protein (1994)
The glow of the crystal jelly made by bacteria: GFP, a living marker for cells (Shimomura 1962, Chalfie 1994). Needs Recombinant DNA. Samples: 4 Glow Ink Sac, 4 Glass Bottle. Unlocks GFP making.

chapters.title: Power
text: # Power
Electric machines take current from the power blocks next to them, or joined to them by Copper Wire (up to 64 blocks of wire) or Insulated Cable (four times as far).
Voltaic Pile (level 3, Voltaic Pile): Zinc and copper discs in brine: put zinc and an electrolyte in; powers machines next to it.
Steam Engine (level 3, Steam Engine): Burns fuel with a water bucket in it; blows furnaces with Bellows next to it 200 °C hotter.
Dynamo (level 4, Dynamo): Put it next to a Steam Engine: powers electric machines next to it or joined to it by Copper Wire.
Solar Panel (level 6, Solar Cell): Silicon cells: current by day under open sky; powers machines next to it or joined by Copper Wire.
Nuclear Reactor (level 6, Nuclear Reactor): Burns uranium fuel rods while water touches it; targets in its slots turn into new elements.
Radioisotope Generator (level 6, Radioisotope Generator): Thermocouples round plutonium-238 pellets: steady current with no fuel to feed.
Helium Collector (level 4, Helium from Radium): A sealed lead-glass vessel: radioactive things kept in it slowly fill Glass Flasks with helium.
Lithium-Ion Battery (level 7, Lithium-Ion Battery): Stores current from the dynamos, panels and reactors it is wired to, and gives it back when they stop.
Diesel Generator (level 4, Diesel Engine): Burns diesel, biodiesel, kerosene, gasoline, naphtha or butanol into current: no boiler, no water.
Wind Turbine (level 7, Neodymium Magnets): A direct-drive generator with neodymium magnets: current from the wind, more the higher it stands.

chapters.title: Radiation and Isotopes
text: # Radiation

Radioactive items give off a dose that builds up while you carry them or stand near them. An Electroscope, later a Geiger Counter, measures it. Lead walls, the Hot Cell and the Nuclear Reactor shield what they hold. Some samples decay on the game clock (one game day is a real day for them) and turn into their daughters in your inventory.
# Blue glow

The strongest emitters glow blue in the dark, as Cherenkov light does: radium and stronger in air, and in water also polonium, americium, actinium and pitchblende, brighter. A running Nuclear Reactor lights up its pool, and running accelerators glow too. The glow follows how concentrated the activity is, not how much you have; uranium never glows. Glowing items also glow in their inventory slot.
# Natural isotopes
Every stable element's tooltip lists its natural isotopes, largest first.
# Ratios that change

Uranium (U-235), plutonium (Pu-240), lithium (Li-6), boron (B-10), calcium (Ca-48) and hydrogen (H-2) items show their own ratio. An item at the natural ratio stacks with any other; an enriched or depleted one stacks only with items at the same ratio. Machines mix ratios by mass.
- The Calutron (Calutron Enrichment) splits uranium, lithium or boron into a small enriched cut and depleted tails. Feed the cut back for more.
- Uranium metal with 3% U-235 or more sinters into reactor fuel pellets.
- Plutonium bred in the reactor is weapons grade (6% Pu-240); plutonium from spent fuel is reactor grade.
- Lithium over 90% Li-6 in a reactor's slots turns into tritium, which lights Tritium Lights for ever.
- Boron over 90% B-10 makes control rods: with one in its slots a reactor stops burning fuel while it is full.
- Heavy water from the Enrichment Cascade (feed it ice or snow) lets natural uranium fuel rods burn.

chapters.title: Containers
text: # Glass Flasks

Every liquid and gas item is a stoppered Glass Flask holding 111.1 units. Five glass make four flasks, with no research needed. A machine fills an empty flask from the top slot of its side panel for each liquid or gas it makes; with no flasks there, it stops and asks for them. When a machine, a recipe, a furnace or a research project uses a flask's contents, you get the empty flask back.
# Steel Cylinders and the Compressor

Gas Compression (level 4) unlocks Steel Cylinders and the Compressor. A cylinder holds 1000 units of one compressed gas: nine flasks' worth in one item. Fit a Compressor in one of a machine's two upgrade slots and put empty cylinders in the second slot of its side panel: the machine then fills cylinders with every gas it makes, a cylinder at a time. Liquids still go into flasks. A cylinder of a fuel gas burns like nine flasks.
Machines take cylinders as input like any other item and hand the empty cylinder back.
# Storage Tank

Pneumatic Chemistry (level 3) unlocks the Storage Tank. It holds 16,000 units (144 flasks) of one liquid or gas. Use it holding a filled flask or cylinder to pour it in, holding an empty flask to draw one out, and with an empty hand to read its level. Hoppers work too: put filled or empty containers in from the top or sides, and take what comes out from the bottom. A comparator reads how full it is. Breaking it spills its contents.
# Relief valve

Under the upgrade slots of every machine's side panel is a relief valve. Shut (red, the default), the machine stops when a gas it makes has no empty flask or cylinder, or no room in the output slots. Click it open (green) and that gas is vented into the air instead, so the machine keeps working; gas that finds a container is still kept. Liquids always wait for flasks.
# Tanks

Gas Mains (level 3) unlocks a tank you build as big as you like. Make a closed box of Tank Plates, edges and corners too, round an empty inside from 1x1x1 to 14x14x14 blocks, and set one Tank Controller anywhere in its walls. Every block of the inside holds 16,000 units of one liquid or gas: a 3x3x3 inside holds 432,000. The controller measures the tank once a second; use it with an empty hand to read its size and contents, or what is wrong.

Tank Valves in the shell are its doors. Use a valve or the controller with a filled flask or cylinder to pour it in, or with an empty flask to draw one out; hoppers put containers in from the top or sides and take them from the bottom, and pipes join it. A comparator reads how full it is. A Tank Gauge in the shell, optional, shows the percent in use on its face; set against a Storage Tank, it reads that tank instead.

A tank has at most one gauge. To add one to a finished tank, use the Tank Gauge on one of its plates: the gauge takes the plate's place, facing you, the plate comes back to you and the tank keeps all it holds.

Every tank has a relief valve: sneak and use its controller, a valve or a Storage Tank with an empty hand and the gas in it goes into the air. Liquids cannot be let out. Breaking the controller loses what the tank held; a gap in the shell only stops the tank until you close it.
# Pipes and pumps

Fluid Pipes join machines to tanks: Storage Tanks, Tank Controllers and Tank Valves (a machine touching a tank works the same). A machine sends every liquid and gas it makes down its pipes into the tanks they reach, before it fills flasks, so it needs none; and when its input or reagent slot is empty it draws from them the liquids and gases its reactions use, a flask's worth at a time, with no flask. Pipes hold nothing; a run may be 1,024 pipes long.
A Fluid Pump moves 250 units a tick from the tanks behind it, directly or through pipes, to the tanks in front of it; it faces the way you look when you place it, and a redstone signal stops it.

# Salt water and fresh water

The sea is salt water: the water of every ocean, beach and stony shore, and of lakes in ocean biomes. Rivers and lakes inland are fresh water, as pure as distilled water. They look and behave the same; only a bucket tells them apart (Bucket of Water or Bucket of Seawater), and a glass bottle fills from fresh water only. In the Geological world no river rises in a desert or badlands, though one from wetter land can run through them.

Two fresh water sources make an endless fresh source between them, and two salt sources a salt one. A fresh source and a salt source always make salt water, and the fresh source turns salt too. Fresh water poured into the sea becomes sea water.

Rare brine springs on dry land, ringed with a white salt crust, hold brine with 26% salts: a Salt Pan dries a bucket of it to about eight times the salt of a bucket of seawater. Brine makes no endless source.

Desalination (level 2) unlocks the Seawater Still. Put in seawater, fuel and empty flasks: it boils the water off into flasks of fresh water and leaves common salt and bittern. Eight flasks of water around an empty bucket make a Bucket of Water.

chapters.title: Machine Upgrades
text: # Upgrade slots

Every machine has two upgrade slots at the bottom of its side panel. An upgrade works once its owner has researched it; two of the same count once. Upgrades marked fuel-fired do nothing in electric machines.
- Compressor (Gas Compression, level 4): fills Steel Cylinders with the gases the machine makes.
- Output Pusher (Automatic Mill, level 3): moves the machine's products into a chest, barrel or hopper next to it. It never feeds another machine directly.
- Regenerator (Regenerative Furnace, level 4): a fuel-fired machine loses half as much heat, so it burns less fuel and heats up faster.
- Refractory Lining (Basic Refractories, level 4): a fuel-fired machine can run 150 °C past its own limit, if its fuel and Bellows can reach that.

- Gas Recovery Hood (By-Product Recovery, level 4): the liquids and gases the machine would vent (carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, hydrochloric acid and others) go into flasks or cylinders instead. Steam and mixed gases such as coal gas are still vented. Caught gas never stops the machine: with no container or room, it is vented after all.

- Mechanical Stirrer (Electric Motor, level 4): works through the charge 50% faster. Its engine burns a quarter more fuel while the charge reacts, or its motor draws extra current in an electric machine.

- Catalyst Bed (Catalyst Beds, level 5): reactions over a solid catalyst (iron, nickel, platinum, platinum-rhodium, vanadium pentoxide, cobalt-manganese bromide) run twice as fast: ammonia, the contact process, nitric acid, coal hydrogenation, reforming, nylon and more.
- Conveyor Belt (Buna Rubber, level 5): an Output Pusher on a rubber belt; it moves finished products four at a time instead of one.
- Foam Lagging (Styrene and Polystyrene, level 6): a machine whose limit is 300 °C or less loses 70% less heat.
- Sterile Air Filter (Penicillin, level 6): the Fermentation Barrel, Vinegar Vat, Deep-Tank Fermenter and Bioreactor make 10% more product. The Deep-Tank Fermenter will not run without one.

chapters.title: Farm and Fat
text: # Rendering and soap

Rendering (level 1) unlocks the Soap Kettle. Meat, bones, eggs and milk go in; the kettle simmers them at 80 to 150 °C. Tallow floats off, and the meat and bone left over come out as Protein Meal, which cows, sheep, goats, pigs and chickens eat and which composts well. Tallow with string makes Tallow Candles: light 12, smoky, and they burn away three days after you place them.

Soap Boiling: put tallow or vegetable oil in the kettle and wood ash in the reagent slot for soft soap, with glycerol in flasks. Hard Soap (level 2) uses soda ash instead, or turns soft soap hard with salt.

Use a bar of soap to wash: you are Clean for ten minutes, and Clean washes off the Hunger of rotten flesh and raw chicken. With dyed leather armour in your other hand, the soap scrubs the dye out instead. Soap with wool or a bed in the crafting grid washes it white.
# Oil, leather and mash

Oil Pressing (level 1): the Oil Press squeezes pumpkin, melon, wheat and cocoa seeds and sunflowers cold. Vegetable oil fills flasks; the Oil Cake left is cattle feed. Tallow and vegetable oil also burn as fuel.

Pit Tanning (level 1): the Tanning Pit turns flesh and hides into leather with no crafting grid, slowly: four rotten flesh make one leather in about three game days. Put oak or spruce logs in the reagent slot for their tannin; the Spent Tan Bark left burns as fuel. Alum Making (level 2) gives potash alum, and two rabbit hides with one alum taw into leather in the crafting grid.

Mashing (level 1): the Fermentation Barrel turns the starch of wheat and potatoes into sugar and then alcohol. Starch Sugar (level 3) does the first step faster with a little sulfuric acid in the Digestion Vat. Sweet Oil of Vitriol (level 2): ethanol distilled with sulfuric acid in the Alembic gives diethyl ether.
# Fertilizer

Superphosphate (level 3) dissolves bones or phosphate rock in sulfuric acid; Gas Liquor (level 3) washes ammonia out of the Coke Oven (keep flasks in its flask slot) and the Lead Chamber turns it into sulfate of ammonia. Use either fertilizer on farmland: for the next eight harvests the crop on it grows half again as fast and a ripe harvest gives one more of its crop.
# Rubber

Rubber trees grow wild in jungles (jungle, sparse jungle and bamboo jungle). Their leaves drop saplings, and the sapling grows anywhere, but a rubber tree gives latex only in a jungle. Vulcanization (level 3) unlocks the Tree Tap: fix it to the side of a rubber log and use it with an empty Glass Flask; it fills one flask every five minutes and holds four. Hoppers can feed it empty flasks from above and take latex from below. Outside the jungle it reports the wrong climate.

In the Vulcanizer, latex with sulfur in the reagent slot cures into vulcanized rubber at 130 to 160 °C; without sulfur it only dries to raw rubber. Vulcanized rubber makes Sneakers (your steps make no vibrations, and magma and turtle eggs don't notice you) and Rubber Wheels: use them on a minecart and it runs 25% faster.

chapters.title: Coal Tar and Medicine
text: # Coal tar

Tar Distillation (level 3): with it researched, the Coke Oven catches the tar of the coal in flasks (keep empty flasks in its flask slot), about one flask per 13 coal. The Tar Still cuts coal tar into benzene, toluene, phenol (carbolic acid) and anthracene, and leaves coal tar pitch. Pitch with gravel and sand makes Tarmac, a road block as fast as Asphalt. Benzene, phenol, tar and pitch all burn as fuel. Nitrobenzene (level 3) nitrates benzene in the Digestion Vat, and Aniline (level 4) reduces it with iron.
# Dyes

Prussian Blue (level 2) unlocks the Dye Vat: rotten flesh or meat with green vitriol in the reagent slot makes the pigment, and the vat turns it into blue dye, 8 to an item. The coal tar dyes give 32 vanilla dyes to a flask: Fuchsine (aniline and white arsenic, magenta), Picric Acid (phenol and nitric acid in the Digestion Vat, yellow) and Alizarin (anthracene and caustic soda in the Autoclave, red). Put the dye in the Dye Vat to get vanilla dyes.
# Infection and medicine

A hit from a zombie, husk, drowned or zombie villager infects you 1 time in 200, and eating rotten flesh 1 time in 100; being Clean halves both. An Infection lasts a game day with Weakness and Hunger. Untreated, it clears up on its own 7 times in 10; the other times it turns to Sepsis, 1 damage every 10 seconds until you die. Carbolic Soap (Antiseptic Surgery: phenol and hard soap) and Aspirin (level 4: phenol in the Autoclave with soda ash, then acetic acid in the Digestion Vat) cure an Infection before it turns. Only Sulfa Drugs (level 5) and the antibiotics of level 6 cure Sepsis. Milk cures neither. The game rule periodicElementsInfection turns infection off.
Aspirin also clears Nausea and Mining Fatigue and gives 10 seconds of Regeneration. Ether Anaesthetic (ether on wool), used on a zombie villager whose cure has begun, halves the time the cure takes.
# Explosives

Dynamite (level 4): glycerol from soap boiling, nitrated cold (5 to 25 °C) in the Digestion Vat, gives nitroglycerin; with sand and paper it makes dynamite, and four sticks with string make a Mining Charge. Light it with flint and steel or redstone: after 4 seconds it breaks every block in a 5x5x5 cube that is weaker than obsidian and every one of them drops. With mobGriefing off it only hurts what stands near. Cordite (level 4) kneads nitroglycerin with smokeless powder; Cordite Cartridges fire from the Breech-Loading Rifle 25% harder and without smoke.
# Crops and pests

Bordeaux Mixture (blue vitriol, quicklime and water) sprayed on a crop or berry bush keeps it from washing out or wilting in the dark, and berry bushes stop scratching. Insect Powder: the Oil Press grinds oxeye daisies to pyrethrum, and an Insect Spray hurts spiders, silverfish, endermites and bees 4 blocks ahead.
# Vacuum Pump

Vacuum Distillation (level 4) unlocks the Vacuum Pump upgrade: in an Alembic, Tar Still, Soap Kettle, Crystallizer, Salt Pan or Refinery Still, every reaction runs 100 °C cooler, so the machine heats up sooner and loses less heat.

chapters.title: Industrial Organics
text: # Carbide and acetylene

Calcium Carbide (level 5): quicklime with coke in the fuel slot of the Electric Arc Furnace fuses into carbide at 1800 °C and more. In the Digestion Vat with water in the reagent slot, carbide gives acetylene (keep flasks, or cylinders and a Compressor, in the vat) and leaves slaked lime.

The Carbide Lamp (brass, glass, carbide and a water bucket) gives light 14 held in either hand or worn on the head, for half an hour. Use it with calcium carbide in your pack to refill it; an empty lamp stays whole.

Oxy-Acetylene Welding: craft a Welding Torch from an acetylene and an oxygen cylinder, a steel ingot and a copper ingot. Hold a damaged metal tool or piece of armour in your other hand and use the torch: one ingot of its own metal from your pack mends a quarter of it, with no experience. The torch does 64 welds; craft it again with fresh cylinders to refill it.
Nitrolime: carbide in the Lime Kiln at 1000 to 1150 °C with nitrogen in the reagent slot takes up the nitrogen as calcium cyanamide, a fertilizer.
# Fertilizer from the air

Urea Synthesis: ammonia in the High-Pressure Reactor at 170 to 200 °C, with carbon dioxide in the reagent slot (catch it from a Lime Kiln or Fermentation Barrel with a Gas Recovery Hood). Prilled Fertilizer unlocks the Prilling Tower, an electric machine: ammonia with nitric acid becomes ammonium nitrate, and urea with PK Blend (superphosphate and potash) becomes NPK Prills.
Nitrolime, urea and ammonium nitrate work on farmland like superphosphate. NPK Prills make the crop grow twice as fast, for eight harvests, each giving one more of its crop.
# Plastics and rubber

Formaldehyde: methanol over silver in the Ostwald Converter at 600 to 700 °C. Bakelite: phenol with formaldehyde in the reagent slot, in the Autoclave at 150 to 200 °C. Four Bakelite make four Bakelite blocks, brown, or black, red, green, ivory or amber with a dye. Bakelite also cases a Geiger Counter in place of brass.
Neoprene: acetylene with hydrochloric acid in the High-Pressure Reactor. A full neoprene Wetsuit gives Dolphin's Grace in water, and no piece of it lets the cold of powder snow in.

Buna Rubber, with no jungle: ethanol over the catalyst in the Cracking Unit at 380 to 450 °C gives butadiene; benzene with ethylene in the reagent slot at 550 to 600 °C gives styrene; butadiene with styrene in the Digestion Vat at 40 to 60 °C gives Buna rubber. It makes Rubber Wheels and the Conveyor Belt upgrade.
# Explosives

TNT: toluene from the Tar Still, nitrated in the Digestion Vat. One TNT with three paper makes three blocks of vanilla TNT. Four TNT, a steel ingot and string make a Demolition Charge: lit like a Mining Charge, it breaks a 3x3x3 cube of anything but bedrock, obsidian included, and drops it all.
# Fermentation, fuel and medicine

Acetone Fermentation: wheat or potatoes in the Fermentation Barrel, with calcite in the reagent slot, ferment to acetone, butanol and a little ethanol instead of sugar. Biodiesel: tallow or vegetable oil in the Soap Kettle at 40 to 150 °C with methanol in the reagent slot. Biodiesel and butanol run the Diesel Generator and burn in furnaces.
Sulfa Drugs: aniline with ammonium sulfate in the Digestion Vat gives sulfanilamide. Use it to cure an Infection at either stage, Sepsis included.

chapters.title: Life Sciences
text: # Antibiotics

Penicillin (level 6) unlocks the Deep-Tank Fermenter, an electric machine that runs only with a Sterile Air Filter. Glucose with milk in the reagent slot (for its lactose) grows penicillin at 20 to 37 °C; Streptomycin takes protein meal in the reagent slot instead. Either antibiotic cures an Infection or Sepsis and makes you immune to Infection for 20 minutes. Use penicillin on a zombie villager with Weakness and its cure begins, with no golden apple. The tank's Spent Mycelium is fertilizer.
# Pesticides

DDT: benzene with chlorine in the Digestion Vat. A DDT Duster used on the ground leaves it deadly to spiders, silverfish, endermites and bees for three game days; chickens on it lay half as often. Weed Killer (2,4-D, from phenol and chlorine) kills flowers, ferns, vines, bushes, saplings and leaves around the block, but spares grass and crops. Pre-Emergent (atrazine, from ammonia and chlorine with coke in the High-Pressure Reactor) keeps grass and mycelium from spreading onto the ground for ten game days. Each sprayer has 16 uses and works 4 blocks round.
# Plastics

Styrene and Polystyrene: styrene in the High-Pressure Reactor. Eight polystyrene round a flask of methane make Foam Lagging; four polystyrene and methane make four Insulation blocks, and ice or snow touching Insulation never melts.
# Explosives

Plastic Explosive: formaldehyde and ammonia make hexamine, and hexamine nitrated cold makes RDX. Two RDX, a copper ingot, a steel ingot and string make a Shaped Charge: place it against a wall and light it, and it bores a 1x1 tunnel 16 blocks deep through anything but bedrock. ANFO: six ammonium nitrate, diesel, paper and string make an ANFO Charge that breaks a 9x9x9 cube of rock; three blocks in four drop.
# Radiation countermeasures

Potassium iodide (sodium iodide from kelp with potash salt in the Crystallizer) cuts the dose from fission products by 40% for a game day. A Prussian Blue Capsule (Prussian blue and protein meal) cuts it by a quarter. Amifostine (level 7) halves the harm of all radiation for an hour.
# Biotechnology

Recombinant DNA (level 7) unlocks the Bioreactor (it needs an integrated circuit). It ferments cellulose from logs, leaves or straw into ethanol, glucose into PLA, and protein with vegetable oil into the mRNA Vaccine, seven game days with no Infection. Its Biomass is fertilizer. PLA makes flower pots and item frames, and composts.

Glyphosate: formaldehyde with phosphoric acid in the High-Pressure Reactor. Field Clear kills every plant round the block, crops too, except wheat grown from Tolerant Seeds (eight wheat seeds round a glyphosate). Tolerant wheat also grows a tenth faster.

chapters.title: Mining Tools
text: # Hammers and excavators

Quarry Hammers (level 2) teaches the Sledgehammer (five ingots round a stick, over a stick) and the Excavator (three ingots and two sticks), in steel and every later tool metal. Each breaks a 3x3 square across the face you hit, at three tenths of the speed, and wears one point per block. Sneak to mine a single block. Only blocks the tool is right for and no harder than the one you aimed at break; nothing with an inventory or a machine ever does; the drops go straight into your pack.
# Blasting

Rock Blasting (level 2): four black powder, paper and string make two Blasting Charges. Lit with flint and steel or redstone, one breaks a 3x3x3 block of stone and drops all of it; dirt, wood and machines are spared.
# Drills and bits

Every drill needs a bit: hold the bit in your other hand, sneak and use the drill. The bit sets what it can mine and how fast (tungsten steel 8.5, high-speed steel 10, cemented carbide 12, diamond 13) and wears one point a swing. Enchant the bit, not the drill; a fitted bit lends the drill its enchantments, all but Mending. Sneak and use with no bit in your other hand to change mode. A drill pays 1.5 kJ per point of hardness of each block: 2.25 for stone, 4.5 for deepslate.

Rock Drill (level 4): the Air Compressor, an electric machine, fills Steel Cylinders with Compressed Air, no Compressor upgrade needed. The Pneumatic Rock Drill burns one cylinder per 600 kJ (about 400 stone) and gives back the empty; it mines one block, a 1x3 tunnel or 3x3, and slows you while you hold it.
# Battery tools
Lead-Acid Battery (level 4): the Battery Pack holds 1,500 kJ. Join a Charging Bench to the wire and use the pack on it; it fills at up to 5 kJ a tick.
Rotary Hammer (level 5) is the rock drill on a pack, with no slowness. The Chainsaw (level 5) fells a whole tree, up to 128 logs, for 3 kJ a log.
The Heavy Mining Drill (level 6) adds a 5x5 mode and a vein mode that follows one ore up to 32 blocks; on a lead-acid pack it slows you.

The Lithium-Ion Pack (level 7) holds 6,000 kJ, is drawn first and lifts that slowness. Ore-Seeking (level 7): in vein mode, use the Heavy Mining Drill on an ore to read the vein's size and elements before you dig.

chapters.title: Exploration
text: # Camping

Hide Tent (level 1): six leather over three sticks make a Tent. Sleep in it as in a bed to pass the night, with no monsters near; it never moves your spawn point. Sneak and use it to strike it and take it with you.
# Backpacks

Leather Backpack (level 1): 27 places for anything but backpacks and shulker boxes. Use it to open it, or press B (Controls) with it anywhere in your pack. While picking up is on (sneak and use to switch), the plant specimens (saplings, seeds, flowers, leaves, mushrooms) and minerals (ores, raw ores, gems, crystals) you walk over go into it first.
Nylon Backpack (level 6): the same with 54 places.
# Traps

Hunting Nets (level 1): five string make a Rope Net. Throw it at a small animal (chicken, rabbit, pig, sheep, cat, fox, parrot, bee, frog and the like) to catch it, and throw the full net to let it out where it lands; the net drops there either way. It wears a little with every catch.
Animal Cage (level 3): the Steel Cage holds any animal, a cow or a horse too, and never wears out. No trap takes monsters, villagers, bosses, ridden animals or another player's pet.
# Finding your way
Explorer's Compass (level 2): sneak and use it to choose a biome, one after another; use it to find the nearest within 6400 blocks. The needle then points there and the tooltip gives the place.
# Lights
Electric Cap Lamp (level 5): wear it and it gives light 15 that follows you, on 0.25 kJ a second from a battery pack in your pack. Without charge it is dark.

Sodium Street Lighting (level 5): set a Sodium Lamp on a fence or wall and run copper wire to the lamp or to the foot of its post. Lit, it gives light 15 and no monster spawns by itself within 24 blocks; it takes 1 kJ a second.
Night Vision (level 6): Night Vision Goggles give night vision and outline monsters within 32 blocks, even through walls, on 0.1 kJ a second.
White LED (level 7): the LED Lamp keeps monsters away within 40 blocks on 0.4 kJ a second, and the LED Spotlight Helmet adds a beam that lights the spot you look at, up to 32 blocks away.

chapters.title: Animals of the World
text: # Wild animals

Every biome has two to four animals of its own, and they spawn only there. Most run from you; large ones fight back when hit. Only the Deathstalker Scorpion hunts you, at night, and the Golden Poison Frog poisons a bare hand that touches it.
# Breeding
Feed two animals of a kind the food they like to breed them. Away from their climate they breed three times more slowly; a greenhouse heated or cooled to their climate lets them breed as usual.
# What animals give

Animals in a pen (a fence within 4 blocks) drop Manure now and then: use it on a plant like bone meal, or burn it. Rub arrows on a Golden Poison Frog to tip up to 8 with poison. A glass bottle on a Deathstalker Scorpion or a Gila Monster draws its venom, once in five minutes. Ostriches lay eggs as big as four hen's eggs.
# Small animals

Insects and worms are items and blocks. Digging dirt or grass now and then turns up an Earthworm, and shearing white mulberry leaves a Silkworm. In swamp water a Medicinal Leech may latch on and slowly bleed you: salt takes it off and gives you the leech.
A Worm Bin (planks round dirt) takes an earthworm; feed it leaves, plants, seeds or manure and it gives Humus, a fertilizer.
Sericulture (level 1): the Sericulture Tray takes silkworms; feed it white mulberry leaves and it gives Silk Cocoons, which smelt into Silk Thread.

Cochineal grows on cactus in deserts and badlands, and the Lac Insect on jungle logs; colonies appear near you and spread. Use a ripe colony to scrape it; use what you scraped on another cactus or jungle log to start a colony.
Carmine (level 2): cochineal in the Dye Vat gives carminic acid, a red dye.
Shellac (level 3): sticklac in the Soap Kettle gives shellac.
Antivenom (level 4): scorpion venom, salt and a glass bottle make Antivenom; drink it to cure poison.
Hirudin (level 5): leeches in the Digestion Vat give hirudin. Exenatide (level 7): Gila Monster venom in the Bioreactor gives exenatide.
# Forests, fields and rivers

Pheasants and Mallards lay eggs now and then, and a mallard sometimes leaves Duck Down. A Red Deer sheds an Antler every day or two; ground, it gives bone meal. Wild Boars drop bristles, which with a stick and a copper ingot make a brush. Sturgeons give caviar and isinglass.

The European Hedgehog keeps pests off crops within 4 blocks. The Eurasian Beaver eats willow bark and builds dams of sticks and mud in shallow water near it. Peruvian Boobies leave guano on the shore, up to half a block deep.
Guano (level 3): guano in the Digestion Vat gives saltpetre.
Galalith (level 5): the casein of milk in the Digestion Vat, with formaldehyde in the reagent slot, gives galalith.
# Cold forests and mountains

Reindeer and Yaks give milk in a bucket, and shears take wool from a Yak or an Alpaca; four make a block of wool. Reindeer shed antlers like red deer. Reindeer Lichen grows near you in snowy lands; reindeer eat it.
Brown Bears raid full beehives and bee nests next to them. The Eurasian Lynx hunts rabbits. The Stoat turns white where it is cold.
# Seas and coasts

Ringed Seals and Walruses give blubber, and walruses ivory; render blubber for lamp oil. Herring, Cuttlefish and the Crystal Jelly go in a bucket; the jelly glows and stings. Cuttlefish give sepia ink (brown dye) and cuttlebone. The Greenland Shark's meat is poisonous raw: cook or smoke it into hákarl. A glass bottle on a Horseshoe Crab draws its blue blood, and the crab lives on. Green Crabs drop crab shell.

Pearl Oysters grow on sand under warm seas near you; break one for oyster shells and, now and then, a pearl. The Sperm Whale cannot be hunted. Ambergris from its gut washes up on beaches now and then, and very rarely a whale strands on a beach and dies there, leaving spermaceti and blubber. Spermaceti and string make a candle.
Tyrian Purple (level 2): murex snails in the Dye Vat give purple dye.
Vitamin D (level 5): shark liver in the Digestion Vat gives vitamin D3. Chitosan (level 6): crab shells in the Digestion Vat give chitosan.
LAL Test (level 7): horseshoe crab blood in the Digestion Vat gives Limulus lysate. GFP (level 7): crystal jelly tissue in the Bioreactor gives green fluorescent protein.
# Animal Compendium

A book and a feather make the Animal Compendium. Carried in the hotbar, it names the animals you know. Look at an animal for a second within 16 blocks, catch it in a trap, or pick up a small one to note it; use the book to read about them, biome by biome. Systema Naturae (level 3) adds scientific names, On the Origin of Species (level 4) each animal's evolution, and The Red List (level 6) its status.

chapters.title: Field Atlas
text: # The Field Atlas

Surveying (level 1): leather, three paper and carbon ink make the Field Atlas. Carry it anywhere in your pack and it draws the land within 24 blocks of where you walk, in rough four-block strokes. Use it to open the map: drag to move, scroll to zoom, right-click to add or remove a marker (8 at first). Without a compass you only know roughly where you are. Surveying also unlocks the vanilla map recipe.
# Compass and coordinates
Magnetic Compass (level 2): the map shows north and an arrow at your exact place; while you hold the Atlas a compass bar runs along the top of the screen. It also unlocks the vanilla compass recipe.

Quadrant and Astrolabe (level 2): the Atlas shows Z (how far north or south you are), a scale bar, and draws 48 blocks around you. Portolan Charts (level 2): sneak and use the Atlas with paper in your other hand to make an Atlas Copy; whoever uses the copy adds all of it, markers too, to their own Atlas.
Marine Chronometer (level 3): the Atlas shows X and Y as well, on the map and on the compass bar.
# Surveying from the air and the rock beneath
Hot-Air Balloon (level 3): a Survey Balloon (wool, charcoal, string and planks) draws 128 blocks all round at once, and is used up.
Triangulation and Theodolite (level 3): the Atlas draws block by block, with relief shading and a contour line every 8 blocks of height, and holds 32 markers.

Geological Map (level 3): the Atlas looks up to 24 blocks under the soil of every column you pass and notes the first rock. Switch the Rocks layer on with the button at the top right; the bar names the rock under the cursor.
# Prospecting, radiation and radio

Diamond Core Drill (level 4): steel, a stick and a diamond make the Core Drill. Use it on the ground: the chat lists every rock and ore down to the bottom, and the Ores layer of the Atlas marks the chunk. Ores you mine are marked too.

Mapping Radioactivity (level 4): every electroscope reading goes on the Radiation layer, from green (background) to red. Geiger Survey (level 5): with a Geiger counter in your pack, the radiation where you walk is logged by itself.

Magnetic and Seismic Prospecting (level 5): the Prospecting Magnetometer reads the 7x7 chunks around you. The Anomalies layer shows magnetic ground (iron, nickel, cobalt, chromium) in blue and dense ground (other ores) in orange, against the survey's own background; it does not name the ore.
Radio Direction Finding (level 5): a Radio Transmitter shares your markers and its own place with every player within 512 blocks who knows radio; they show in blue on that player's Atlas.
# Radar, satellites and GPS

Radar (level 6): a Radar Station on the wire network shows you, on the Atlas, every creature and player within 96 blocks of it: players white, hostile creatures red, the rest green. With a Handheld Radar in your pack a minimap sits at the top left of the screen, with what the set sees within 48 blocks; the N key hides it.

Airborne Gamma Spectrometry (level 6): radiation readings are split by isotope (U-238, Ra-226, Th-232, Cs-137 and more) on the Isotopes layer, coloured by the main source. Fly with a Geiger counter, or stand 16 blocks above the ground, and the 3x3 chunks below are read at once.

Satellite and Tracking Station (level 7): use a Satellite on a Launch Pad under open sky to put it in orbit. A Tracking Station with power then maps the land round itself onto your Atlas, from the station outwards, 512 blocks each way in a day, even where nobody has been: land never loaded is drawn from its height and kind of country. Each satellite (up to four) makes it faster.
Multispectral Scanner (level 7): the satellites also note the rock of the land they map, and ores within 8 blocks of the surface, where the land is loaded.

Global Positioning System (level 7): a GPS Receiver in your pack shows the minimap anywhere, with your coordinates. Where you die goes on the Atlas as a marker, and a middle-click on a marker sets a route: its distance under the minimap and its bearing on the compass bar.

chapters.title: Tree Compendium
text: # The Tree Compendium

A book and any sapling make the Tree Compendium; no research is needed. Keep it anywhere in your hotbar and the top-left corner of the screen names the biome you stand in, and the tree you look at once you know it.

To note a tree, look at its log, leaves or sapling for a moment from up to 8 blocks away, or fell it, while the book is in your hotbar. Walking into a biome notes the biome. Use the book to read: biomes on the left, the trees of each one on the right, with what each tree is, how tall it grows, where it grows and what it gives.
Sneak and use the Compendium with a book in your other hand to make Compendium Notes; whoever reads them adds every tree and biome in them to their own Compendium.
Species Plantarum (level 3): each tree shows its scientific name, its family and where it grows wild in the real world, after Linnaeus (1753).
Geography of Plants (level 3): each biome shows its climate, and the corner of the screen shows it too, after Humboldt (1807).
The Red List (level 6): each tree shows how threatened it is in the wild, after the IUCN (1964).

chapters.title: Plant Compendium
text: # The Plant Compendium

A book and any small flower make the Plant Compendium; no research is needed. It works like the Tree Compendium: keep it in your hotbar and the top-left corner names the biome and, once you know it, the plant you look at. Flowers, grasses, ferns, shrubs, crops, water plants and the plants of lush caves are all in it.

To note a plant, look at it for a moment from up to 8 blocks away, or pick or harvest it, while the book is in your hotbar; plants under water are noted the same way. Use the book to read: biomes on the left, the plants of each one on the right.
Compendium Notes copy both books at once: whoever reads them gains every tree, plant and biome in them.
Species Plantarum (level 3): each plant shows its scientific name, its family and where it grows wild in the real world.
Geography of Plants (level 3): each biome shows its climate, in this book as in the Tree Compendium.
The Red List (level 6): each plant shows how threatened it is in the wild.

chapters.title: Mineral Compendium
text: # The Mineral Compendium

A book and a flint make the Mineral Compendium; no research is needed. Keep it in your hotbar and the top-left corner names the rock you look at once you know it. Look at a rock for a moment from up to 8 blocks away, or mine it, to note it. Use the book to read: groups on the left, the rocks of each one on the right.

A rock's composition shows only once you have analysed it: hold a Magnifying Lens and look at the rock for 2 seconds. Even then the book names only the elements you know; the rest is summed as "other" and fills in as your research finds new elements. Until analysed, natural rocks, ores and plants hide their composition in their tooltips too; made things keep showing it.
Compendium Notes copy all three books at once.
De re metallica (level 2): each ore shows its mineral and the depths where it is found, after Agricola (1556).

Theory of the Earth (level 3): each rock shows its class (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic) and how it forms, and the book groups rocks by class, after Hutton (1788). In the Geological world the corner of the screen also names the formation you stand on.
Thin Sections (level 4): each rock shows the minerals it is made of, after Sorby (1858).
X-ray Diffraction (level 5): each mineral shows its formula and crystal system, after the Braggs (1913).

chapters.title: Trees of the World
text: Every land biome has five trees of its own, real species that grow wild there. A sapling grows only in the biomes its species comes from: anywhere else it stays a sapling, and bone meal does nothing. Its tooltip names those biomes.

Fruit and nuts drop from the leaves now and then. Strip a log with an axe to peel off the bark where the bark is the useful part. Fix a Tree Tap to a tree that gives sap or resin: liquids need an empty flask, hard resins drop straight into the tap.

In the machines: pine resin in the Alembic gives turpentine and rosin; cinnamon bark, camphor wood, eucalyptus leaves and sandalwood give their oils in the Alembic; cinchona bark in the Digestion Vat gives quinine; brazilwood in the Dye Vat gives red dye. Oily fruit goes to the Oil Press, sweet fruit to the Fermentation Barrel.

In the temperate woods: tap sugar and red maples for maple sap and boil it down in the Salt Pan for sugar. Strip cork from the cork oak and willow bark from the white willow; the Digestion Vat draws salicin from the bark, and later turns it into salicylic acid. Cedar of Lebanon gives cedar oil in the Alembic. The lacquer tree gives urushi lacquer. Yew leaves hold a trace of taxol, which only the last level can extract.

In the cold and on the mountains: larches, firs and pines fill the taigas; the coast redwood and the giant sequoia, the tallest and the biggest trees on Earth, grow only in the old growth spruce taiga. Above the tree line, dwarf pines, junipers and the arctic willow creep low and take root in stone, gravel and snow. Tap the balsam fir for Canada balsam, the clear cement of lens makers, and the Scots pine and the larch for pine resin.

Fruit trees: mango, orange, lemon, papaya, avocado and cashew in the tropics; cherry, plum, peach, apricot, fig, pomegranate, almond, pistachio, hazel and pecan in the temperate lands. The Parana pine of southern Brazil gives edible seeds and resin. Lemons carry citric acid, which the Digestion Vat crystallizes out. Horse chestnuts are not for eating.
# Jungle
- Mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla): timber
- Brazil Nut Tree (Bertholletia excelsa): Brazil Nut from the leaves
- Brazilwood (Paubrasilia echinata): wood with Brazilin
- Sapodilla Tree (Manilkara zapota): Sapodilla from the leaves; Chicle from a Tree Tap
- Andiroba (Carapa guianensis): Andiroba Seed from the leaves
- Brazilian Rosewood (Dalbergia nigra): dense firewood
- Avocado Tree (Persea americana): Avocado from the leaves
- Kapok Tree (Ceiba pentandra): Kapok Fiber from the leaves
# Bamboo Jungle
- Teak (Tectona grandis): timber
- Cinnamon Tree (Cinnamomum verum): Cinnamon from the bark
- Camphor Laurel (Cinnamomum camphora): wood with Camphor
- Sal Tree (Shorea robusta): Dammar from a Tree Tap
- Nutmeg Tree (Myristica fragrans): Nutmeg from the leaves
- Mango Tree (Mangifera indica): Mango from the leaves
- Orange Tree (Citrus sinensis): Orange from the leaves
# Mangrove Swamp
- Black Mangrove (Avicennia germinans): wood with Sodium Chloride; leaves with Sodium Chloride
- White Mangrove (Laguncularia racemosa): wood with Tannin; wood with Sodium Chloride
- Buttonwood (Conocarpus erectus): dense firewood
- Nipa Palm (Nypa fruticans): Nipa Fruit from the leaves; Palm Sap from a Tree Tap
- Buriti Palm (Mauritia flexuosa): Buriti Fruit from the leaves
# Old Growth Pine Taiga
- Ponderosa Pine (Pinus ponderosa): Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
- European Larch (Larix decidua): Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
- Eastern White Pine (Pinus strobus): Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
- Lodgepole Pine (Pinus contorta): Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
- Scots Pine (Pinus sylvestris): Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
# Sparse Jungle
- Acai Palm (Euterpe oleracea): Acai Berry from the leaves
- Babassu Palm (Attalea speciosa): Babassu Nut from the leaves
- Copaiba (Copaifera langsdorffii): Copaiba Balsam from a Tree Tap
- Cinchona (Cinchona officinalis): Cinchona Bark from the bark
- Oil Palm (Elaeis guineensis): Oil Palm Fruit from the leaves
- Lemon Tree (Citrus limon): Lemon from the leaves
- Papaya (Carica papaya): Papaya from the leaves
# Savanna
- Baobab (Adansonia digitata): Baobab Fruit from the leaves
- Gum Arabic Tree (Senegalia senegal): Gum Arabic from a Tree Tap
- Marula (Sclerocarya birrea): Marula Fruit from the leaves
- Shea Tree (Vitellaria paradoxa): Shea Nut from the leaves
- Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus globulus): leaves with Eucalyptol
- Cashew Tree (Anacardium occidentale): Cashew from the leaves
# Savanna Plateau
- Pequi Tree (Caryocar brasiliense): Pequi from the leaves
- Barbatimao (Stryphnodendron adstringens): wood with Tannin
- Yellow Ipe (Handroanthus serratifolius): dense firewood
- Jatoba (Hymenaea courbaril): Copal from a Tree Tap
- Sandalwood (Santalum album): wood with Santalol
- Parana Pine (Araucaria angustifolia): Parana Pine Seed from the leaves; Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
# Windswept Savanna
- Baobab (Adansonia digitata): Baobab Fruit from the leaves
- Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus globulus): leaves with Eucalyptol
- Dragon Tree (Dracaena cinnabari): Dragon's Blood from a Tree Tap
- Frankincense Tree (Boswellia sacra): Frankincense from a Tree Tap
- Myrrh Tree (Commiphora myrrha): Myrrh from a Tree Tap
# Wooded Badlands
- Pinyon Pine (Pinus edulis): Pine Nut from the leaves; Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
- Utah Juniper (Juniperus osteosperma): Juniper Berry from the leaves
- Ponderosa Pine (Pinus ponderosa): Pine Resin from a Tree Tap
- Gambel Oak (Quercus gambelii): Acorn from the leaves; wood with Tannin
- Mountain Mahogany (Cercocarpus ledifolius): dense firewood
# Beach
- Coconut Palm (Cocos nucifera): Coconut from the leaves
- Tropical Almond (Terminalia catappa): Tropical Almond from the leaves; leaves with Tannin
- Casuarina (Casuarina equisetifolia): dense firewood
- Screw Pine (Pandanus tectorius): Pandanus Fruit from the leaves
- Sea Grape (Coccoloba uvifera): Sea Grapes from the leaves
- Cashew Tree (Anacardium occidentale): Cashew from the leaves
# Desert
- Date Palm (Phoenix dactylifera): Date from the leaves
- Mesquite (Prosopis juliflora): Mesquite Pod from the leaves; dense firewood
- Joshua Tree (Yucca brevifolia): timber
- Saxaul (Haloxylon ammodendron): wood with Sodium Chloride; dense firewood
- Argan (Argania spinosa): Argan Nut from the leaves; dense firewood
- Pistachio (Pistacia vera): Pistachio from the leaves; dense firewood

chapters.title: Shrubs and Greenhouses
text: # Shrubs
Shrubs grow wild in every land biome, three to five kinds in each, and like the trees each grows only in its own biomes. A bush takes about twenty minutes to ripen; bone meal speeds it up.

Right-click a ripe bush to pick what it gives: leaves, seeds, fruit, roots or stems. It stays planted and ripens again. Shears on a grown bush cut a cutting to plant; some seeds, like peppers and jojoba, can be sown too. Breaking a bush gives a stick or two, and its harvest if it was ripe.
# Greenhouses

In a greenhouse a shrub or a tree sapling grows far from its biomes. A greenhouse is a closed room, up to 32 by 32 blocks and 32 high, entered only by a door or a trapdoor, with a roof all of glass or glass panes over every part of it. Shrubs need two blocks of height; a tree grows only if it fits whole under the roof (common trees 9 to 12 blocks, tall ones 15 to 18, giants about 26).

An unheated greenhouse is temperate: tea and the shrubs and trees of temperate lands grow in it. A lit Greenhouse Heater on the floor or against a wall makes it warm, for tropical and desert plants too (Heated Greenhouse, level 2). Load the heater by using fuel on it; it burns a coal in about five minutes.
# Thorns
Brambles, blackthorn, roses, gorse, capers and gooseberries prick whoever walks through them, a little at a time, like a sweet berry bush. Foxes and bees go through unharmed.
# Teas

Two leaves or flowers and a water bottle make a tea. Each gives a mild effect for a short while and cures one bad effect, as milk cures them all: black tea gives haste and cures mining fatigue; rooibos, resistance (hunger); hibiscus, fire resistance (weakness); rose hip, absorption (poison); lavender, regeneration (nausea); rosemary, night vision (blindness); heather, speed (slowness); Labrador tea, health boost (wither).
# Hydrangea

The hydrangea flowers pink in limy soil and blue in acid soil, where aluminium dissolves into it. Use aluminium sulfate or alum on it to make it flower blue, and quicklime, slaked lime or chalk to make it pink again.
# Cold greenhouses

Arctic and alpine plants need a cooled greenhouse. A running Greenhouse Cooler on the floor or in a wall makes it cold (Cold Greenhouse, level 4). It melts ice put in it: a snow block lasts 30 seconds, ice 2 minutes, packed ice 18 minutes, blue ice an hour. With no ice it runs on current from a copper wire, 20 kilowatts. Temperate plants grow in a cold greenhouse too; a heater and a cooler in the same room cancel out.

chapters.title: Crops and Genetics
text: # Crops

Twenty crops grow wild in the world: a ripe plant standing on grass or sand that does not grow. Break it for its seeds (cassava gives stem cuttings) and sow them on farmland like wheat. Rice needs water right next to its farmland. Coffee and alfalfa stay planted: right-click them when ripe to pick them, and they grow back.

Each crop likes some climates (warm, temperate or cold). Elsewhere it grows at half speed, never not at all. In a dry land (desert, savanna, badlands) a field that is not fully watered also grows at half speed, unless the crop is a dry-land one (cotton, castor, alfalfa, sorghum). A heated greenhouse counts as warm.
# Genes

Every plant, the vanilla crops too, carries six genes, two copies of each, one from each parent. They act from the first sowing; research only lets you see them. The useful form of each gene and how it shows:
- C, Cycle: cc plants ripen about 30% sooner (recessive: Cc looks normal).
- P, Yield: one P is enough for a 30% chance of one more crop at harvest (dominant).
- R, Disease resistance: one R makes rust four times rarer (dominant).
- D, Drought tolerance: dd plants grow at full speed in dry lands without water (recessive).
- F, Cold tolerance: one F lets a crop of warmer lands grow at full speed in the cold (dominant).
- I, Pest resistance: one I makes caterpillars four times rarer (dominant).

Seeds from shops, villages and vanilla stacks have the plain forms (CC pp rr DD ff ii). Wild plants carry the useful forms, often hidden in one copy: that is where improvement comes from. Wheat seeds from grass are sometimes wild too.
# Crossing

When a plant ripens it takes pollen from a ripe plant of its kind within 2 blocks: maize, hemp, rapeseed, alfalfa, turnip, carrot and beetroot do so 80% of the time, the others only 5% (they pollinate themselves). Each seed then gets one copy of each gene from the mother and one from the father, at random. One gene in 500 mutates. Cassava and potato are planted from pieces of the plant: they copy it exactly. Seeds with different genes do not stack.

Domestication (level 1) teaches the Seed Lens: use it holding seeds in your other hand, or on a crop, to see their traits. A plant that carries a recessive form in one copy looks plain: only its offspring tell.

Animal Husbandry (level 1): the Feeding Trough holds a stack of feed and feeds the animals within 6 blocks that eat it: grown animals breed and the young grow up faster. Cows, sheep and goats eat alfalfa, oats, barley, sorghum and turnips; pigs maize, cassava, soybeans and turnips; chickens grain; horses oats and alfalfa.

Crop Rotation (level 2): soybeans, beans, indigo and alfalfa harvested ripe leave their farmland fertilized. Natural Dyes (level 2): the Dye Vat makes blue dye from indigo leaves and red dye from madder root.

Plant Hybridization (level 3): the Pollination Brush takes pollen from a ripe plant; brushed onto a plant of the same kind, anywhere, it makes that plant the father of its seeds. Tobacco Wash (level 3): three tobacco leaves and a water bottle wash the caterpillars off the crops around where you use it.
Mendel's Laws (level 4): the Seed Lens shows each gene's two letters, so Cc tells apart from CC. Cross two Cc plants and a quarter of the seeds are cc.
# Pests and diseases

A plant growing among more than 20 of its kind in a 9 by 9 square can catch caterpillars or rust. It stops growing, gives one crop less and passes it to its neighbours. Mixed fields catch nothing. Break it, or use Tobacco Wash or Insect Spray against caterpillars (crops on DDT ground never catch them) and Bordeaux mixture against rust. The game rule periodicElementsCropPests turns pests and diseases off.
# Modern breeding

Mendel's Laws also teaches the Crossing Notebook: use it on seeds held in your other hand, then on the other parent's seeds. It writes out, gene by gene, what share of the seeds of that cross will show each trait.

Silage (level 4): the Silo turns maize, sorghum and alfalfa, put in by hand or from a hopper, into silage, one every 5 seconds; a hopper below takes it out. A trough of silage lasts twice as long. Nitrogen Fixation (level 4): Inoculant used on soybeans, beans or alfalfa gives their roots rhizobia: harvested ripe, they leave their farmland strongly fertilized.

Hybrid Maize (level 5): a seed of two different pure lines (lines with two equal copies of every gene) is an F1 hybrid: it grows and yields 20% more, but its own seeds lose it. The Seed Lens marks hybrids and pure lines. Balanced Feed (level 5): maize kernels, oats, protein meal, bone meal and salt make 4 feeds every farm animal eats: the young grow twice as fast and parents are ready to breed again sooner.

X-ray Mutagenesis (level 5): the Seed Irradiator X-rays seeds put in it (40 kJ a seed from piles or dynamos joined to it). 3 seeds in 10 die; each gene copy of the rest mutates 20 times as often as in nature. Sow them all and keep the rare useful ones.

DNA Double Helix (level 6): the Seed Lens shows every trait. Wheat and rice carry a seventh gene, S, Stature: ss plants are semi-dwarf and on strong fertilizer (NPK) yield half again as much, the Green Revolution. Wild wheat from the grass of cherry groves sometimes carries s.

Gamma Garden (level 6): the Cyclotron makes a cobalt-60 source from cobalt with heavy water in the reagent slot; eight lead round it make the Gamma Garden. Crops that ripen within 6 blocks of it give seeds that mutate 20 times as often. It is radioactive: keep your distance.

DNA Sequencing (level 7): the DNA Sequencer reads the whole genome of seeds used on it (20 kJ a seed). PCR (level 7): the Thermocycler tests each seed against a marker seed (sneak-use a seed on it to set the marker): seeds with every useful trait of the marker go to a hopper below, the rest to hoppers at the sides (10 kJ a seed).

Transgenesis (level 7): with a gene construct in your other hand, the Gene Gun used on a crop puts the gene in it; half the shots take. Bt: caterpillars never take it. EPSPS: Field Clear spares it. Golden Rice (rice only): its grains carry vitamin A and can be eaten raw. DREB: drought tolerant. Seeds inherit a transgene from either parent. CRISPR (level 7): the CRISPR Kit writes the useful form of one gene into both copies of a crop; sneak-use it to choose the gene.

chapters.title: The Geological World
text: # The Geological world

Geological is a world type (chosen by default when you create a world). The ground is built from real rock: each region belongs to a province, and the province decides the rocks, the relief, the caves and the ores. Biomes and climate are the vanilla ones and do not depend on the rock.
# Provinces
- Cratons: old shields of gneiss and granite, with diorite and granite domes. Banded iron, pegmatites and quartz veins with gold.

- Sedimentary basins: flat layers of sandstone, red mudstone, shale and limestone (calcite) over the old basement. Coal, oil shale, red-bed copper and, in dry climates, evaporites (salt, borax, saltpetre). Caves and sinkholes (dolines) follow the limestone bands; under sea level they are flooded.

- Volcanic provinces: basalt flows with thin tuff beds, lava tubes with skylights, basalt necks. Under the basalt lies a band of peridotite with chromite and pentlandite, and granite below it. Porphyry copper and molybdenite, fumarole sulfur and rare kimberlite pipes with diamonds.
- Mountain belts: folded layers where two provinces meet, with a core of granite and gneiss deep inside and rare slivers of peridotite (ophiolites). Porphyry copper, gold and wolframite.
- Oceans: smooth basalt over stone.
# Volcanoes

Stratovolcanoes rise in the volcanic provinces and along the edge of the mountain belts: cones a hundred or two hundred blocks wide, built of andesite and tuff in layers, with bare rock and ash (gravel) near the top. The crater holds a lake. A few volcanoes are still active: their crater holds lava over magma instead of water. Fumaroles with sulfur open in and around the crater.
# New rocks

Shale, gneiss, peridotite, kimberlite and laterite are new blocks. Each one breaks into its cobbled form (Silk Touch keeps the rock), smelts back into the rock, and makes polished blocks, stairs, slabs and walls in the crafting table or the stonecutter. Ores grow in the rock they really form in: a block such as Iron Ore (Shale) drops the same as the plain ore.
# Soils

The dirt follows the rock under it. Terra roxa, a dark red soil, covers the volcanic provinces and the humid tropics; chalky soil, pale and full of lime, lies over the limestone of the basins. Both are dirt: grass and trees grow on them and a hoe turns them into farmland. Granite and the mountains keep coarse dirt.
# Surface hints

Red patches of rusty rock (gossan) lie over many deposits. Rivers that cross a gold, tin, coltan or diamond deposit carry ore-bearing gravel downstream: break it to get the ore. The Magnifying Lens and the Mineral Compendium name every rock and ore variant.

chapters.title: Structures
text: # How structures work

Some machines grow into structures. Build a shell of casing blocks round an empty inside and set the machine in its wall, facing out: it becomes the controller and works with the size of the whole structure. Alone it works as before. The bigger the structure, the faster it works and the less heat it loses per item: speed = (inside volume / smallest volume)^0.85, so doubling the volume gives x1.8, not x2.

The controller measures its structure once a second and shows it on its screen. If a block is missing, the screen names it and its layer, and red sparks mark the spot while you hold the Field Guide. Structure Ports set anywhere in the shell let hoppers in and out as the machine's own sides do: from above into the input, from below out of the products, from the sides into fuel and the other slots.

To build one, sneak and use its controller with the Field Guide in your hand: the smallest structure is drawn round it in translucent blocks (orange the shell, grey the ports, red the Tuyere, blue the tower) and each block you place takes its place. Do it again to hide it.
# Blast Furnace stack

A Charcoal Blast Furnace set in the wall of a column of Refractory Brick. The inside is 1x1 to 3x3 blocks and 3 to 10 high, open at the top; the floor and every wall block, corners too, are refractory brick, a Tuyere or a Structure Port. A Tuyere in the bottom layer is required: Bellows or a Steam Engine against it blow the whole stack. Fired with coke it runs 100 °C hotter than the furnace alone.

Every three Fuel Channels burn rods and make current like one reactor alone; a bigger core loses fewer neutrons at its edge, so each rod lasts longer.

The core must be critical (k 1 or more). Enriched rods are critical in any core. Natural rods, with heavy water in the slots, only in a big one: 7x7x7, 8x8x6, 9x9x5 and larger, like the CANDU reactors. Above k 1.3 the chain reaction runs away unless a Boron Control Rod is in the slots. If it runs away, or the water goes, the reactor scrams: the rod is lost and radiation leaks round it for half a day. It never explodes.
